items.body:
Special edition of Sun Ra’s classic ‘Lanquidity’, for the 25th anniversary of the label. If yr looking for a way to penetrate Ra's intimidating catalog, "Lanquidity" is a precious wormhole that gives a taste of the jazz pioneer's astral weirdness without letting it overwhelm. Transformative shit, really.

Released in a tiny edition back in 1978, "Lanquidity" is Sun Ra's attempt at cultural reconciliation. It's the ultimate flex, finding the Arkestra alien absorbing contemporary pop elements (disco, funk, soul) into his canon, before spitting them out as further cosmic strings in his pan-universal bow. The playability of "Lanquidity" has given it legs: before its reissue in 2000, the album had hardly been heard, but was spoken about in hushed tones. A couple of decades later, it's an established classic, putting Sun Ra's talent into full view and quieting some of the sprawling galaxy-brain oddness that alienates some listeners.

Recorded by Philly Jazz boss Tom Buchler (who penned enlightening liner notes about the recording experience), "Lanquidity" has Sun Ra fronting a band of over fourteen players, including Marshall Allen on alto sax and John Gilmore on tenor. Intriguingly, he also ropes in not one but two guitarists, giving the album its "Bitches Brew"-adjacent fusion fuzz, but it's the overdubbing of disembodied voices and layers of Arp and Minimoog that puts these tracks into a category all of their own. The mood Sun Ra creates is truly planetary (just flick to the album's terrifyingly tripped 'There Are Other Worlds (They Have Not Told You Of)' for proof) and while he certainly makes concessions with his stylistic choices, the pop shell is merely a Trojan horse for his vanguard forms.

Classic.
items._genre: avant-garde jazz / cosmic jazz / fusion / experimental
items._cn_summary: 这张1978年的专辑是Sun Ra对流行元素的策略性吸收，将迪斯科、放克与灵魂乐编织进其宇宙美学的框架中。乐队由十四位乐手组成，包含双吉他配置，产生类似Bitches Brew的融合质感，而离散的嗓音采样与Arp、Minimoog合成器的叠加层才是真正区别于常规作品的核心。整体氛围呈现行星尺度的空间感，流行外壳实为承载其先锋形式的特洛伊木马。在Sun Ra庞大的目录中，此作是相对易于进入的入口，既展现了艺术家的核心视野，又避免了部分作品过于散漫的怪异性对听众的排斥。专辑曾以极小印量发行，后经再版获得经典地位。

items.body:
Supremely exquisite new album of baroque-pop and dream-spun stylings from emergent Greek harpist-composer Sissi Rada, tipped if yr on the line from Svitlana Nainio to Lena Platonos, CV & Jab to Niecy Blues, Laurie Anderson to Jan Steele & John Cage’s ‘Voices and Instruments’ alltimer​...

‘Nana Butu’ is the deeply impressive 5th solo suite by classically trained string player, Sissi Rada, whose skills have been sought out for record and stage by everyone from Lena Platonos to Brian Eno and Jay Glass Dubs in the past decade. It was with her Stroom debut ‘Aporia’ (2024) that Sissi’s magick really registered with our ears, at least, and since then her captivating blend of virtuosic instrumental tekkerz and hallucinatory sound design palette has been confirmed to these ears/eyes in a former Manchester mortuary and on the divine ‘Demeter In Aexone’ LP for Gomma’s Kryptox subsidiary. Now on a dozen parts bejewelled with extended lines of crystalline melody and unfurling like a waking dream, Sissi doubles down on her music’s transcendent enigma beside a cohort of mutually enchanting spars - Charis Karantzas, Jay Glass Dubs, Oï les Ox, and Theodor Milkov - for a real inception of a record; irrefutable proof of a sorceress at work. 

On sides dealing with the “fragile, tangible world of mortals” and “the cosmic beyond, home to souls and celestial beings”, Sissi assumes a psychopomp role to guide listeners between thematic dualities of life/death, light/dark, waking/dreaming, wth typically low-key yet compelling vision. Never showy, and intimate to uncanny degrees, the album foregrounds her voice more than ever. Variously alloyed with alchemic instrumental touches, and diffused in shapes bent between genres, her voice floats with rare elegance against electro-acoustic contours, variously channelling a sort of avant folk R&B bliss like Clara La San meets Sinead O’Connor on the glyding Reese bass of opener ‘Ave Verum’, or blooming in avant-jazz harmonies like Julee Cruise channelling Alice Coltrane in ‘FOGO’, and that’s only the 1st pair. 

It’s a whole pinch-yourself dream herein, plucking on fantasy theatric strings with ‘Benches’, and coming off like some golden era Hollywood diva in her titular centrepiece. The 2nd half serves to suspend disbelief for the duration, subtly ushering a more unearthly feel with a sublime duet of bittersweet jazz harmony and nagging discordance on ‘MI-MI’, and slipping deep into fantasy realms like Xexa jamming with Meredith Monk on the deliquescent Disney trip ‘FOMO’, before mutual spirit and avant-chanteuse Oï les Ox chimes in on an all-too-short ‘Message’ and it continues to surprise until the end, with the tart vignette ‘Your Order at 4’ calling to mind Beth Gibbons reframed by Rashad Becker, and ‘Wooden Floors’ signs off with a flourish of prepared piano of AFXian virtues. Your ears won’t deceive you - or if they do, in the best way - on this utterly absorbing gem by a real standout in the contemporary field.
items._cn_summary: 希腊竖琴演奏家兼作曲家Sissi Rada第五张个人专辑，以十二个乐章构建出一场介于生死、光明与黑暗、清醒与梦境之间的通灵之旅。她将古典竖琴的精湛技艺与电声纹理、迷幻声景编织在一起，人声首次成为前景，与器乐形成炼金术般的融合。专辑呈现巴洛克流行与梦幻编织的美学，曲目从开篇的低调前卫民谣蓝调，到爵士和声与不和谐音的甜蜜对峙，再到幻想剧场般的幽深意境，层层递进。与多位跨界合作者（Jay Glass Dubs、Oï les Ox等）的互动拓展了声场维度，准备钢琴与电子质感在末段交汇，展现出当代古典、实验音乐与另类流行之间罕见的贯通力。

items.body:
So this is a bit special… thanks to the efforts of a NIN forum, Coil's legendary and incredible 'Recoiled' versions of Nine Inch Nails are finally given an official release.

Although never properly released - other than excerpts used in David Fincher's Se7en - the tracks have been in circulation for some years now yet never collected for a full release like this. It includes five extended and thorough revisions of some total NIN classics in just under 40 minutes, all crafted in the pre-Ableton era and ranging from a gutted and strung out version of 'Closer [Unrecalled]' - as used in Se7en - to a blinding deconstruction of 'The Downward Spiral [A Gilded Sickness]', to an extended and industrialized take on 'Gave Up [Open My Eyes]', and two reworks of 'Eraser' - a beatless 'Reduction', and a previously unheard, technoid 'Baby Alarm' mix with bespoke effects crafted from, you guessed it, a baby alarm.

For many, it's debatable whether this is what the late great Peter Christopherson and Jhonn Balance would have wanted - as with all their posthumous releases and reissues - but it's really hard to argue when the thing is in your hands. Highly recommended.
items._genre: industrial / darkwave / experimental electronic / EBM / post-punk
items._cn_summary: 这张合作专辑收录了Coil对Nine Inch Nails经典作品的深度解构与再创作，涵盖五首时长总计近四十分钟的扩展版本，制作于Ableton软件普及之前的纯硬件手工年代。曲目跨度极大：从曾用于大卫·芬奇《七宗罪》配乐的剥离去骨版《Closer》，到彻底拆解的《The Downward Spiral》，再到工业化长篇演绎的《Gave Up》，以及《Eraser》的两版变奏——其中无节拍的缩减版与以婴儿监视器改造为效果源的technoid混音尤为特别。整体手法延续Coil一贯的工业暗黑美学与声音实验逻辑，对原始素材进行拆解重组而非简单混音，呈现出既忠于原作又完全异化的听觉景观。这类跨阵营的工业合作在地下场景中具有罕见的深度与历史价值。

items.body:
One of Masami Akita's most unexpected collaborations, 'Strange City' is surprisingly legit, pieced together from licensed samples and framed by Akita's visceral distortions.

You have to wonder how it might have sounded if Sun Ra and Akira had come face to face, but 'Strange City' is about as close as we'll get. An official release made with the blessing of Irwin Chusid, executor of the Sun Ra catalog, the album was made from "rare and unreleased tracks from the Sun Ra archive", which Akita puts through the meat grinder, as expected.

What we actually hear from those original recordings is tough to gauge. On 'Livid Sun Loop', there's a burst of drums and horn for a few moments before the squeals are snuffed out almost completely by Akita's own shrieking white noise. Soon, the sounds are buried beneath dense layers of distortion and fritzed oscillations - audible if you train your attention to cut between the wall of noise, but left as a trace, followed by Akita. 

On the epic flip 'Granular Jazz Pt. 2', Akita allows more room for Sun Ra's recordings, paring down his blaring cacophony to a soft racket and allowing the horns and rattling drums to at least interact with his arsenal of machines. Now that's jazz.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是日本噪音大师Merzbow（秋田昌美）与已故先锋爵士先知Sun Ra的跨界合作。Merzbow从Sun Ra档案中获取了罕见且未发行的原始录音片段，经过官方授权后，将其送入他标志性的噪音处理设备中进行彻底解构。在《Livid Sun Loop》中，原始的鼓点和铜管声在短暂浮现后即被刺耳的白噪音淹没，密集的失真层和振荡器将源头声音仅留为痕迹。而在长达二十分钟的《Granular Jazz Pt. 2》中，Merzbow有意识地收敛了自己的声墙，让Sun Ra的号角与打击乐得以与电子噪音形成真正的对话与互动。整张专辑既是采样艺术的极致实验，也是对两位艺术家精神相遇的另类想象。

items.body:
In the 15+ years that have elapsed since 'Loop Finding Jazz Records' first shuffled out of his ambrosially dusty speakers, Jan Jelinek's most famous album has acquired an almost mythical status. Originally released via Pole's defunct Scape imprint, it now finds new life via Jelinek's own Faitiche label, for a new generation to marvel at one of the finest examples of loop-based electronic music typical of the early noughties.

Taking what reads like a pretty austere set of ingredients, Jelinek's technique revolves around a trio of elements which consist of second long cuts of 1960's-70's jazz recordings, the loop-finding modulation wheel (do your homework!) and the Moiré effect; albeit rendered in the acoustic as opposed to the image and spectral domains.

If all this sounds a bit academic, be assured that on record it is anything but; as crumbling edifices of mealy rhythms slowly pulse into life and swirl around your head like snow storms clashing with a dust devil. Taking sediments of fathom deep static then skimming the best stuff from the top, Jelinek opens through the dampened echoes of 'Moiré (piano & organ)' wherein a slow-motion thrum of spiraling clicks, rustles and analogue tones conspire to give the impression of recondite perspectives that extend well beyond the constituent elements.

Elsewhere, 'Rocky in the Video Age' instills a gratuitously optimistic blush to the aquatic micro-sound ebb, 'Moiré (Strings)' is a perfect companion to Basinski's disintegrating tape archive, whilst 'Them, Their' represents an aural crease so sleight you can only catch its distinctive gleam from the corner of your eye.
items._cn_summary: Jan Jelinek 的代表作由 Faitiche 厂牌再版发行，原作曾由 Scape 厂牌出版。整张专辑的核心手法是将六十至七十年代爵士录音切成一秒左右的片段，通过循环搜索调制轮与声学领域的莫尔效应进行加工，形成碎片化的微观声响景观。文章描述了不同曲目的具体质感：《Moiré (piano & organ)》以潮湿回响开启，缓慢脉动的螺旋状咔嗒声与模拟音色营造出深远的透视感；《Rocky in the Video Age》在微弱的水下微观声波中带有乐观色调；《Moiré (Strings)》的质感近似 Basinski 逐渐崩解的磁带档案；《Them, Their》则轻巧得几乎只能用眼角余光捕捉其光泽。评论强调，尽管制作理念看似学术，实际听觉体验却充满诗意的颗粒感与流动感。

Commissioned by the French state, "Senderos de luz y sombras" (or pathways of light and shadow) is the latest transmission from Beatriz Ferreyra, who composed the half-hour, 16-channel piece between 2016 and... more
items.body:
Decades into a career that began at Paris's fabled GRM, Argentinian innovator Beatriz Ferreyra is still worlds ahead, transmuting environmental recordings and snake-like foley rustles into cosmological whispers that ponder the universe's big questions. 

Commissioned by the French state, "Senderos de luz y sombras" (or pathways of light and shadow) is the latest transmission from Beatriz Ferreyra, who composed the half-hour, 16-channel piece between 2016 and 2020. She was inspired by astrophysics (specifically the time before the Big Bang), and the world of the unconscious mind, and dedicates the composition to the memory of sound sculptor Bernard Baschet, electro-acoustic innovator Bernard Parmegiani, and her friend Carlos Pellegrino. 

If you've heard her  GRM releases, or Room40's two essential anthologies ("Echos+" and "Canto+"), then you'll no doubt already be intrigued - that material helped to cement Ferreyra's well-deserved place in the canon, her work speaks for itself. Ferreyra's fathoms-deep tape manipulation experimentation has inspired countless artists, from Keith Fullerton Whitman and Jim O'Rourke to Debit and Valerio Tricoli, and this latest full-length just reminds us how open-minded and freely experimental her compositions can be.

The piece is split into two side-long chunks, both of which tremble with eerie uncertainty. 'Senderos abismales' is gusty and effortlessly psychedelic, using carved-up field recordings to suggest familiarity before sending us wheezing into the cosmos. Ferreyra doesn't need much: the distinct sounds of tyres on wet tarmac, wind whispering in the distance, and distant birdsong are sculpted into a giddy, multidimensional lattice of chiseled sonics and ponderous philosophy. Her confidence is key here, and she never needs to do too much; the negative space is just as important as any chaotic moments, and the tiny breaths of harmony - from icy winds, spectral processing, or something else entirely - sound as if they're provoking life in a vacuum. Comparatively 'Senderos del olvido' is more upbeat, beginning with exploded star sound design that shifts thru a sci-fi spectrum without using any of the usual pneumatic sound effects that have become customary.

Ferreyra is too thoughtful to rest on obvious cultural totems. Her vision of cosmic emptiness is strikingly human; when she voyages into the abstract, her gurgling, digitally-reduced textures only remind us of the soul behind the complex processes. And just as her '70s tape music allowed us to feel an emotional connection to music that was too often lost in academia's back rooms, "Senderos de luz y sombras" reminds us that the same is true of contemporary computer music. If you enjoyed the run of recent Roland Kayn reissues, this one's gonna be absolutely required listening.
items._genre: electroacoustic / field recording / experimental / sound art
items._cn_summary: 阿根廷裔作曲家贝亚特丽斯·费雷拉自巴黎GRM起步，深耕磁带与电子声学实验数十年。这张由法国国家委约的专辑以16声道呈现半小时作品，灵感来自大爆炸前的天体物理学议题与无意识世界。素材取自轮胎碾过湿地、风声、远距鸟鸣等日常录音，经过雕刻般的声音塑形，编织成多维度的声响晶格。她用极少素材达成宏大效果，负空间与混沌时刻并重，冰冷的风声与幽灵般的频谱处理在真空中唤起生命感。整张专辑体现了学院计算机音乐中罕见的人文温度，将宇宙虚空转化为可感知的情感场域，是当代电子音乐中难得的深度之作。

items.body: As the title indicates, Noise Trip Explosion is intense. I am tempted to label it unrelenting or something of the sort, but it does not quite reach that intensity of harsh noise, at least for extended stretches. Rather, the noise on this trip is glitchy, it comes in starts and stops, and Nolan Hildebrand's mixer feedback and live electronics are complemented by saxophones, violins pianos, guitars and percussion. Notably, it is also composed through a series of sound inputs and generative graphic scores that leave ample room for intermittent relenting and pivots. (For more on the set-up, loops, and feedback that produce the graphic scores and the musicians’ interactions with them, see the liner notes.) Rather, Nosie Trip Explosion is diverse in sound and personnel. Hildebrand occupies the roles of musician and composer, and is joined by a coterie of musicians, whose own backgrounds run from contemporary classical to jazz and free jazz to abandoned warehouse micro-noise. Hildebrand himself is even absent on the surprisingly open but still dark Raw Data Speed Demons, where Roan Ma deploys both electronics and violin, and the final summative track DADA BENDER, which is a percussion sextet “with fixed media.” Having listened to a lot of noise recordings that fall short, sometimes in ways I cannot quite put my finger on, I can vouch for Noise Trips Explosion . Hildebrand is never just making noise, as if anyone really can outside of some predetermined system. Rather, he acknowledges, constructs, analyzes, and reconstructs his choice (sometimes generated in and adaptive in real-time) system to great effect and clamor. What is more, some of the strongest tracks, such as knurl cracked green and the 16+-minute portals II (everywhere and everything right now) (which must be a nod to Everything, Everywhere, All at Once ), stray from delight in sheer electro-noise especially through the more traditional instrumentation of the rest of the crew. Portals II in particular draws noise into harsh free jazz and vice versa with real aplomb. DADA BENDER is also a standout in its collision of percussion and beats with glitched circuitry and cartoon effects that amalgamate into a techno-dystopian march of shrapnel, laser sounds, and other sonic dregs, and scraps of various live percussion to prod it along. This particular bender, and this entire sonic trip, is well worth the abandon. A side-note on the artwork: it is a glitchy and colorful throwback to earlier days of home computer/internet abstractions and fits the deceptively scrappy aesthetic of the album perfectly. Noise Trip Explosion is available on CD and as a download via bandcamp: Noise Trip Explosion by Nolan Hildebrand Email This BlogThis! Share to X Share to Facebook
items._genre: experimental / free jazz / noise / electronic / contemporary classical
items._cn_summary: 诺兰·希尔德布兰德以混音器反馈与现场电子为核心，串联萨克斯、小提琴、钢琴、吉他与打击乐，借助声音输入与生成式图形谱构建乐曲结构，使噪声在即兴框架中以断续、跳跃的方式展开。专辑跨越硬核自由爵士与电子噪声的边界，部分曲目如长达十六分钟的portals II将传统乐器演奏融入电子噪声洪流，形成双向渗透；终曲DADA BENDER以打击乐六重奏叠加故障电路与卡通音效，构筑出技术反乌托邦式的行进感。乐评特别指出希尔德布兰德并非随意制造噪音，而是在自创系统中持续拆解、重组声音选择逻辑，使得整张作品在多样乐器编制与人员组合下保持统一的美学方向。封面设计采用早期家用电脑互联网美学，与专辑质朴而锐利的声响气质相呼应。

items.body: Discipleship, as practised at Terry Riley’s Kirana East, turns the Western paradigm of individual creativity on its head, argues Ryan Meehan The train had taken me some three hours out of Tokyo to Kobuchizawa, a hamlet in Japan’s Southern Alps – a first taste of countryside quiet beyond the reach of the megacities. My contact meets me at the station: Hiromitsu Hirata, who will serve as my translator for the day, having learned English during his time studying music and philosophy in India. He’s also the newest of Terry Riley’s disciples at Kirana East, the small but vibrant raga school founded by Riley after he relocated to Japan in 2020. Another student and I climb into Hiro’s silver van to reach a house beside a meadow. Through a doorway on the garden deck, we enter a sunlit living room brimming with musical instruments and speaker equipment, where a handful of students are already seated around our instructor Sara Miyamoto. It’s only by chance that I’m able to sit in for this introductory class. Now 91, Riley no longer gives interviews; the lessons he teaches are private, and only for the advanced. But as luck would have it, this basic class falls within the window of my visit to Japan, and Miyamoto has given her blessing to join the circle as an observer. With conversation buzzing around me, I shuffle through a packet of instruction materials written by Riley. I first became acquainted with kirana gharana (a signature music style of northern India) while covering a birthday celebration event held by La Monte Young for the late kirana singer Pandit Pran Nath (see The Wire 443), the guru shared by Young and Riley until Nath’s death in 1996. I’ve sought out Kirana East with a degree of confidence in my understanding of its basic premises. Almost immediately, however, the complications of even this short introduction begin to envelop me in dread. There is the sargam, the Indian equivalent of solfeggio, with its specific proportion of sharps and flats; the gamaks, technical flourishes with which the singer moves between the notes; the all-important alap, the raga’s slow introductory motif, which we will be practising as a group. I am not a student of any substance in this music, I say to myself; I’m not even a musician. My trip here has been an imposition, a gesture of real arrogance. In deepening embarrassment, my eyes scan across the page to a phrase underlined in bold: “In practice, you don’t have to be too concerned with this.” Its placement seems like a pin to pop my ballooning panic, and with my relief comes a convulsion of laughter. When I explain, Miyamoto smiles: “That’s so Terry.” Without much ceremony, the lesson gets underway. Miyamoto guides the group through a series of preparatory exercises. Eyes closed, the mind acclimates to stillness, and with each new prompt – about body and mind; awareness of sound, consciousness, and position within the universe – the suggestion that music might be a parallel domain, a constitutive fabric of reality, begins to seem plausible. Miyamoto’s prompts (as translated into my ear by Hiro) are not unlike those of an especially attuned yoga class, only instead of the repetitions of bodily poses, we begin cycling through clusters of notes at the foundations of kirana singing. Her voice is crystalline, gliding between pitches with precision, polishing the rough edges I hear in my own. A lesson like this requires a curious mixture of discipline and relaxation: one maintains concentration and control over one’s own tone, while at the same time giving oneself over to the larger sonority of the group. It’s challenging and meditative and pleasurable, and before I can get my hands around it, it’s over. Miyamoto first heard raga via an Ali Akbar Khan album in the record collection of her family, whose Japanese musical underground ties are extensive. The studio where she teaches, Hoshi To Niji (Star And Rainbow), was founded by her father in the back of his dental practice, and has hosted decades’ worth of recordings, the most recent among which are some by Eiko Ishibashi and Jim O’Rourke, as well as her own collaborations with Riley. She began her life as a musician playing bass, and first met Riley during his 2017 trip to Japan for an event programmed by her husband. “When I saw Terry’s concert in Japan, I was so shocked how much information the sound included. Just a single note he played from the melodica brought tears to my eyes.” She leapt at the opportunity to take instruction from him. “At the time I didn’t have any idea what ‘disciple’ meant. I was not planning to study raga. I just wanted to keep my life going as a musician.” There’s something poetic about the hazard with which Miyamoto found herself embarking on gurukula, the master-disciple relationship that helps to maintain the classical raga tradition. As disciples of Pran Nath, Young and his wife Marian Zazeela were not above tying his shoes if it meant making his life “more beautiful”. While the demands of discipleship are unique in each case, the underlying devotion is absolute. It amounts to a sacrifice of a notion of personal freedom in exchange for total access to the wisdom and guidance of a venerated elder. “Being a disciple means totally losing my ego,” explains Miyamoto. “I am not the first priority in my life at the moment, and I have to be open for every study from Terry. The outline of myself has totally vanished, and I don’t have to think about that.” The intensity of the gurukula relationship can be unnerving to those on the outside of it. In the Western mainstream, musicians are stars; we glorify the autodidacts, the iconoclasts, the rootless young. By contrast, the late composer Michael Harrison sat beside La Monte Young for nearly a decade, adjusting his guru’s tuning for the performance of The Well-Tuned Piano, a piece Harrison was only allowed to perform once on his own, and then only in private. Young’s closest disciple Jung Hee Choi has described gurukula as “the most demanding long-term art project”. For Hiro, this contrast is a matter of perspective: “We are always educated in modern society as an individual who has the right to choose. We are supposed to have judgement and reasoning. In general, in the Eastern tradition, education is the opposite. When we start, we are blind. We don’t have the ability to choose the path we go. That’s why we need a guru, the one who removes the darkness and shows the path. Because we are not yet able to judge, we should surrender to someone we think trustworthy.” If discipleship remains niche as a way of life, other aspects of kirana hold unmistakable appeal in the Western avant garde, with figures such as Jon Hassell, Don Cherry and Catherine Hennix all taking instruction from Pran Nath during his lifetime. Perhaps this influence is preparing the ground, in some form or another, for its resurgence. This essay appears in The Wire 510. Wire subscribers can also read it in our online magazine library.

items._cn_summary: 这篇乐评来自《The Wire》杂志，记述作者前往日本南阿尔卑斯山区拜访特里·赖利（Terry Riley）于2020年迁居日本后创办的Kirana East印度斯坦尼古典音乐学校的亲身经历。Kirana East教授源自北印度的kirana gharana拉格传统，文章详细描写了入门课程的内容，包括印度式视唱练耳（sargam）、装饰音技巧（gamaks）以及作为拉格开场的缓慢引子（alap）。赖利作为90岁高龄的西方极简主义作曲家兼印度音乐修行者，其教学将传统师徒传承（guru-shishya）模式移植到日本，体现了西方个人主义创作观与东方集体传承精神的碰撞与融合。乐评通过作者从惶恐到释然的心路变化，生动呈现了Kirana East所坚持的冥想式音乐修行理念，文章在日美印三种文化语境中穿梭，展现了世界音乐与实验音乐跨文化对话的独特视角。

items.body: Thalie Némésis is a French artist who together with The Memory Of Snow founded her own label.” Dé(s)figurations” is her latest album, featuring a collaboration with Eva|3 on one track, while mixing and mastering were entrusted to Peter Rainman. The album opens with a powerful composition that recalls Industrial and Goth-Metal, immediately showcasing Thalie Némésis’s enchanting voice. As the record unfolds, it gradually reveals calmer and, above all, more dreamlike pieces, although several of them are punctuated by explosive, heavier climaxes. Her Ethereal vocals act as a guiding force, leading the listener like a mermaid—or perhaps a muse—through a magical sonic landscape. The floating, atmospheric passages often evolve into something almost Cinematic. Towards the end, a growing sense of foreboding takes hold, culminating in a mystical and captivating closing track. Above all, Thalie Némésis is an artist with a distinctive artistic identity—something I find far more compelling than the work of those who simply rely on a predictable ‘copy-and-paste’ formula. (Rating:7). Side-Line covered the release of “Dé(s)figurations” when it came out on Meridian Noir Records in May 2026. Listen to “Ruptures”: Ruptures by Thalie Némésis About Thalie Némésis Thalie Némésis is the solo project of the French musician Nathalie, based in Aix-en-Provence. The project first appeared in 2013 and released early material in 2014, including work with Les Modules Étranges, before a long pause. Thalie Némésis returned with the 2025 EP “Catarsi Apotropaica,” which forms the first half of “Dé(s)figurations.” Nathalie co-founded Meridian Noir Records, a French label for dark alternative music, with Albin Wagener of The Memory of Snow, whose album “Inside” the label released in June 2026. “Dé(s)figurations,” out May 22, 2026 on Meridian Noir, is reviewed above.
items._cn_summary: Thalie Némésis是来自法国普罗旺斯艾克斯的独立音乐人，与The Memory of Snow共同创办了暗潮系厂牌Meridian Noir Records。《Dé(s)figurations》是她的最新专辑，融合工业与哥特金属的能量，同时展开梦境般飘渺的氛围段落。空灵的人声是贯穿全作的主线索，引导听者穿越超现实的声响景观；多首作品在悬浮质感与爆发性高潮之间切换，后半段逐渐引入不祥的预兆感，最终以神秘而迷人的曲调收束。整张专辑展现出鲜明的个人艺术辨识度——既有重金属的冲击力，又有电影化的空间感，与流水线式的类型复制形成鲜明对比。

items.body:
Revisiting their debut album '.After', Tujiko Noriko and Adrian Corker commission a suite of remixes, bringing in Koshiro Hino ov YPY, goat (JP) and KAKUHAN fame, Tashi Wada, DJ Trystero, Shojiro Nakaoka and DJ ojo to put their spin on the source material.

The original album only took Noriko and Corker a couple of days in the studio, but they wired the results to percussionist and arranger George Barton, who took it to the next level. They continue the thought on '.After Again', dishing out the stems to a carefully pruned list of collaborators - artists whose distinctive sounds only extend the original album's sonic universe. And of course it's the YPY version of the album's opening track 'Yasashii Sayonora' that'll have most of y'all chomping at the bit; Hino turns Corker and Noriko's source material to dust, time-stretching Noriko's vocal and zeroing in on the stuttering percussion and rusted turntable loops. Adding his signature jerks, he fills the track with clattering metallic clangs, twisting the voices into downsampled groans from a neighboring cyber-reality.

Tokyo's DJ Trystero opts for a different but similarly unique approach on his two reworks, the "All Frills" remix of 'Toku No Minato' and his "Naive Declension" version of the same track. On the former, he isolates almost indistinguishable elements of the original, setting the ghost traces to a typically deep, dubby groove and on the latter, creates a rugged, gear-heavy jam from the remains. It's actually Nakaoka who provides the weirdest - yet strangely most recognisable - versions, using his custom generative code to match Noriko's voice with whirring interference and warbling digital detritus.
items._genre: experimental electronic / ambient / remix / glitch / abstract
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是对Noriko与Corker首张作品'.After'的再访，以remix合集的形式展开。制作流程颇具层次：原录音在短短数日内完成，随后交给打击乐手与编曲者George Barton进一步加工。重混版本延续这一思路，将原始音轨的stem分发予精心筛选的合作者，每位艺术家以各自独特的声响语言延伸原作的声场空间。Koshiro Hino（YPY）对开场曲的重塑最为抢眼，他将Noriko的人声进行时间拉伸处理，聚焦于断裂的打击节奏与锈蚀的唱机循环，加入标志性的金属撞击质感，将声音拽入一个低采样率的赛博维度。DJ Trystero则对同一曲目提交两个版本，一版将原素材拆解为几乎不可辨的幽灵碎片，置于深邃的dub律动之上；另一版则从残骸中拼凑出粗粝的齿轮质感的jam。Shojiro Nakaoka运用自创生成代码，使人声与旋转的数字干扰形成奇异共振，成为整张专辑中最怪诞却最具辨识度的段落。整体听感横跨抽象电子、低频dub、噪音拼贴与生成算法音乐，适合对声音实验有较高耐受度的听众。

items.body:
War.Poem by Chris Connelly, via Dirter Promotions.

“ "WAR.POEM” was recorded at THE ROCK NOIR studio in 2025/2026 as a reaction to a piece I read on the Israeli military use of FLECHETTE SHELLS in Gaza, this led to a much deeper study of the 20th/21st century history of war. The album was composed entirely using a TAPE O MATIC 710 reel to reel from 1958, a 1960’s mayfaair JVC reel to reel, aa 1965 G.E. solid state portable reel to reel from 1965, a portable 1970’s Panasonic cassette player, a ring modulator as well as various other effects and synths.

The loop that is the basis for WAR POEM ZERO which takes up the whole of side one, happened by accident when I put a reel on the wrong way up, it produced aa sound of such great melancholy and beauty, I just let it play…

This album owes a debt to “SWANSONG” by NURSE WITH WOUND from the album “A MISSING SENSE” where experimental sound is used as an anti war protest.

- Chris Connelly 2026"

You are unlikely to hear a record of such brutal intensity, or indeed authenticity as this. To call it “old school industrial” would be to do it a disservice, but also not THAT wide of the mark. It is packaged sympathetically to Chris’ previous release for the label, the long sold out LP “White Phosphorous”."
items._genre: industrial / experimental / tape music / dark ambient
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Chris Connelly对以色列在加沙使用集束弹壳这一事件的音乐回应，进而延伸至对20至21世纪战争史的深入探究。整张作品完全使用多台古董磁带设备录制，包括1958年的Tape O Matic 710开盘机、1960年代JVC开盘机、1965年G.E.便携式开盘机以及1970年代松下卡带播放器，配合环形调制器与各类合成器及效果器完成。专辑A面整段由一段偶然产生的循环构成——将磁带反向装入时意外获得了极为忧郁与美丽的声音，艺术家随即决定让它自然发展。B面内容承接Nurse With Wound专辑《A Missing Sense》中《Swansong》以实验声响作为反战抗议的思路展开。整体声响具有强烈的暴烈感与原始真实感，难以归入单纯的旧派工业范畴。

items.body:
Essential listening FFO Time Is Away, Jon Collin or the 'Bagpuss' soundtrack, Rory Salter, aka Malvern Brume, confronts cutesy British folk nostalgia on 'For Red Riverbank', using 'The Wind in the Willows' references, sobering newsreel snippets and straight-to-tape acoustic jams to develop a faded image of labour inequality.

Nostalgia is supposed to be digestible - a cultural banana that gives the mind all familiarity without friction. But munch on the same gear for too long and it starts to cause irritation; it's hard not to notice, for example, that the prim Ghost Box-style Gen Z hauntology has reached its logical conclusion. Whatever it was saying about the UK's welfare-era lost futures has not only been photocopied half to death, but it's also been added to the slop machine, spat out as empty "content" that's almost hypnotically nauseating - especially when you consider the state of welfare in 2026. Thankfully, we're not the only people to have noticed; Salter takes aim at the romance of British folk culture on his proper The Sprigs debut, using a framework we'll all be familiar with - Kenneth Grahame's Edwardian children's classic 'The Wind in the Willows'. It's important to note that the book was already steeped in nostalgia when it was first published back in 1908, a reflection on nature in the face of mass industrialization, as the affordable Ford Model T was beginning to appear on roads for the first time. So it's a more complex reference than you might initially figure, and Salter uses this backdrop to root his investigation of British labour history and the very meaning of tradition.

We've all heard remnants of folk music vibrate through the collective consciousness over the years, not least in the wake of the New Weird America movement of the early '00s. And Salter's awareness of these sounds and the perpetual churn that followed is crucial; he doesn't subvert them as such, but repurposes them, hitting on themes and sequences that connect us to the country's soil and textures that help to rub away some of nostalgia's entrancing sparkle. The 12-minute opener 'come along, back home' sounds at first like an old protestant hymn being bellowed through broken pipes and Salter keeps scraping away at history, collaging textured environmental loops with simplistic, almost naive folk songs, peculiar resonances and, occasionally, what sounds like an old recorder. And it's the back-and-forth between gravelly noise and nostalgic naivety that makes 'For Red Riverbank' so inviting. The short, sharp 'Ratty & the moles get to work' is just as jolly as its title, sounding as brittle and evocative as Sandra Kerr and John Faulkner's fluttered folk songs that lifted Oliver Postgate's 'Bagpuss'.

And Salter doesn't just look back through rose-tinted spectacles, he juxtaposes these evocative sounds with sobering recordings of newsreaders, politicians and union leaders, who complete a quite genuine picture of the recent past. Like George Eliot's Middlemarch, that imagined a fictional Midlands town four decades prior to its writing, the inviting idealized setting was a Trojan horse for Eliot's real theme: the 1832 Reform Act that upended the electoral system. Salter employs the same sleight of hand, introducing us to a world we know and love before drip, drip, dripping the politics we so desperately need.
items._genre: experimental folk / hauntology / collage / sound art
items._cn_summary: Rory Salter以The Sprigs之名发行的这张专辑以肯尼斯·格雷厄姆的《柳林风声》为框架，将爱德华时代儿童文学中已存在的怀旧情绪层层剥离。专辑核心策略是将原声民谣即兴、磁带录音、环境音循环与新闻播报、政客及工会领袖的录音片段并置，形成粗粝噪音与天真民谣之间的持续张力。开场曲长达十二分钟，从破碎管风琴般的清教徒赞美诗逐渐演化为拼贴式的声景雕塑。专辑并非简单颠覆民谣传统，而是重新利用其土壤感与质感，以此审视英国劳工史与怀旧工业的当代困境。文中将其置于Time Is Away、Jon Collin等实验民谣谱系中，并与Ghost Box式的新一代hantology形成对照。

It runs like some lost 1980’s private press, tipped FFO early Yves Tumor, Yungwebster, Space Afrika, AYYA... more
items.body:
Perhaps the most interesting PAN in a minute; ‘Lila’ is the label debut from Paris-based Algerian Mohamed Bourouissa, best known as a visual artist but now offering a glimpse into his musical practice for the first time, blending highly unusual ambient pulses with autotuned, low-lit vocals, recorded on the fly using a keyboard, mixer, microphone and effects. It runs like some lost 1980’s private press, tipped FFO early Yves Tumor, Yungwebster, Space Afrika, AYYA, Future, Kareem Lotfy.

Bourouissa’s first solo album finds the 48 year old artist capturing the permeable membrane between Paris' various communities through a dream diary of hazed ambient reflections, cloud rap inversions and bass-heavy club malfunctions. It follows his work over decades incorporating music as a phantom thread of his practice in photography, sculpture, and video, and perfectly conveys a sense of longing and melancholy central to Arabic classical and pop songs mediated via an electronic hypermodernism . The album is an intimate, sometimes unsettling experience, aptly described as “hypnagogic” by PAN, as heard in its tendency to dreamlike slowness and the layered haze of FX and xenharmonic chords that shroud and wreath his melismatic woes. 

The dozen tracks play out through autotuned vocal plumes familiar from work by Ayshay, Rainy Miller or Future, crossed with the type of deep blooz oozing from that superb Taymour x Bareetlblad turn on the diy label earlier this year. Each track taps a different pole into the album's landscape, one beatless, and one filled with machinegun toms and explosive snares. The beatless tracks are peculiarly stirring and the heavier, noisier moments somehow vanish into the same aether. Bourouissa peppers the album with wild twists and turns, hitting a dark alley on the anxiety-inducing 'NMB' and descending corrugated steps to a members-only basement on 'MN'. The relief comes with the title track, a collaboration with Fanigliulo (aka Mushy) that's a tender, hopeful moment -  a clouded love song that injects some hope into the darkness.
items._genre: ambient / experimental electronic / cloud rap / hypnagogic
items._cn_summary: 巴黎阿尔及利亚裔视觉艺术家 Mohamed Bourouissa 首次以个人专辑形式呈现其音乐实践。整张专辑仅凭键盘、混音器、麦克风和效果器即时录制，将环境脉冲、自调音人声与阿拉伯古典及流行音乐的忧郁气质相互渗透，营造出一种介于梦呓与清醒之间的恍惚感。十二首曲目在无节拍氛围与厚重俱乐部节拍之间反复切换，既有尖锐焦虑的低谷，也有与 Fanigliulo 合作的柔软亮色。评论将其描述为失落八十年代私人出版物的气质，融合东方旋律记忆与超现代电子语汇，呈现出跨文化、跨媒介的独特听觉肖像。

items.body:
Autechre's classic second album, 1994.

At last, Warp reissue one of their most loved gems, which Autechre themselves have referred to as conceiving as their “Warp record” - written to complement the label’s early ‘90s ambient/AI catalogue.

Depending on yr perspective, Amber is quite possibly the most beautiful Autechre album. It’s much softer, more atmospheric than the needling electro tones of Incunabula, and also much more approachable, more innocent than the cold, rugged Tri Repetae; like a snapshot of the duo in post-club gouch-out mode, hugging the sofa and chewing their ears in the days before somebody might snap you doing so on their iPhone.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Autechre于1994年发行的经典作品，被厂牌Warp再版发行。两位成员将其定位为向厂牌早期九十年代氛围与人工智能音乐系列致敬的创作，风格比首张专辑更柔软、更具氛围感，也比后来的作品更易接近、更显纯真。整体氛围描绘出俱乐部深夜散场后的恍惚状态，沉迷于沙发与耳机的亲密时光。合成器音景取代了尖锐的电子音色，呈现出温暖而内省的聆听体验。Warp作为独立电子厂牌，延续了其在电子音乐领域一贯的艺术定位。该作介于氛围与智性舞曲之间，是二人作品序列中最柔和的一环，展现了电子音乐在俱乐部文化之外的可能性。

items.body:
All killer, no filler, evergreen compendium of no wave to punk-funk and synth wave from a pivotal era of NYC dance history. Simply too many nuggets to name a fave - a big one for any there at the time, or who got it 2nd hand via LCD Soundsystem and the sound’s whole Y2K resurgence.

‘New York Noise – Dance Music From The New York Underground 1978-82’ was among the most crucial retrospective comps of the early 00's. It would emerge in the wake of LCD Soundsystem’s anthem ‘Losing My Edge’, and an upswell of electroclash to perfectly join the dots between NYC’s late ‘70s, early ‘80s upstarts who adapted punk’s license to bridge rock and dance in mutant new styles which still light a fire under the ass of so many artists bands today, generations later. 

Shake a stick and you’ll hit a minter anywhere across the 16 tunes, from Liquid Liquid’s percolated cowbells on the punk funk blueprint ‘Optimo’ (which lent its title to the legendary club night), to impLOG’s freaky proto-techno bomb ‘Holland Tunnel Dive’, the wiry jump-up chops of The Contortions’ Contort Yourself’, thru the louche synth wave swag of ‘Reduction’ by Bill Laswell’s Material, the no wave yowl of Mars and Theoretical Girls’ stop/start torque, to Alan Vega ov Suicide’s rock ’n roll throwback, ‘Bye Bye Bayou’.
items._genre: no wave / punk-funk / synth wave / post-punk / proto-techno
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑梳理了1978至1982年间纽约地下舞曲场景的关键轨迹，涵盖从no wave、punk-funk到synth wave的多种实验形态。编选以Liquid Liquid的'Optimo'为代表，展现打击乐节奏与funk律动的解构重组；impLOG的'Holland Tunnel Dive'呈现早期电子机械感的techno雏形；The Contortions强调扭曲断裂的身体节奏；Material的'Reduction'带来流畅的合成器律动；Mars与Theoretical Girls则保留no wave的原始张力与噪音棱角。整体选曲跨越多种风格脉络，呈现纽约音乐人如何从朋克出发，将摇滚与舞曲嫁接为全新形态，为后来LCD Soundsystem及electroclash潮流提供了源头参照。

items.excerpt: GbClifford's "Love, Diskito" via Mappa Editions. items.body:
GbClifford's "Love, Diskito" via Mappa Editions.

"There is an abruptness to waking up to the sight of the other person’s back, a quiet violence hidden in the impression of intimacy, that’s leaving an aftertaste of emptiness. The feeling of losing oneself completely in a love that is given but never returned. Or the slower, less immediate one - the gradual disintegration of a world into which so much was once invested.

Love, Diskito is like a worn out overdubbed cassette found in a drawer, with its underlying tracks flickering between contrasting emotional states. Written, produced and mixed by GbClifford, the release follows up on the elusive, multifaceted output of the Prague-based experimental artist, who dresses fleeting glimpses of youthful yearning, sentiment and fragility in the blunt apparel of distortion and immediacy.

Drawing from their idiosyncratic, collage-like approach to music production, GbClifford condenses on Love, Diskito a varied palette of field recordings, samples, distorted instruments and ambient sounds. They resemble doodles in the corner of a school notebook, tightly overlapping with the evocative, minimalistic artwork by Czech artist Kateřina Šípová.

The guidance of GbClifford’s personless, at times highly decomposed vocals modulates the emotional urgency of the recording and reflects on the past. “I’m so close to relapsing, I’m here for you, closer than ever,” echoes in the elusive track So Only Yours, carrying the undercurrents of surrendering to the sole necessity of caring, even at the cost of individual ache. While the album does not forgo its earthbound, bare setting, there is something deeply pastoral and sky-gazing in the layered, multi-pitched vocals, horn-like tones and sense of space that Love, Diskito evokes."
items._cn_summary: 布拉格实验艺术家GbClifford的《Love, Diskito》以拼贴式的制作手法，将田野录音、采样、失真乐器与环境声响压缩在一起，形成一种像被反复翻录的老旧磁带般的声音质地。人声被处理得时而抽象、时而高度分解，以无形的方式承载情感张力，在亲密与疏离、投入与失去之间游走。多层人声叠加出号角般的音色，空间感辽阔而带有田园式的仰望意味。专辑虽扎根于粗粝、裸露的底色，却通过层次与留白展现出开阔的情感维度。整体上，这是一张关于爱的消逝与自我沦陷的概念作品，以低保真质感与解构性制作完成了一次情感与声音的双重实验。

items.body:
After crafting an all-timer with 2008's 'Hazyville', Actress set his sights on the unknown with a futureshock debut for Honest Jon's.

Wheras it's predecessor was composed over a staggered period of many years, Splazsh was fashioned in a fraction of that time, lending a tangible symmetry between shapeshifting tracks that defined and propelled the era. Of the 14 tracks, we'd previously encountered the first two, with the unstable space float of 'Hubble' appearing on a shady Thriller 12" and his remix of Various Production's 'Lost' reminding us that there are some deep cuts in the Cunningham discography.

From here in it's all about that longing, sealing the airlock and initiating pressure sequence with 'Futureproofing', before laying down 'Always Human' - can u even remember a time you didnt know this one? Showing resistance towards any categorisation, 'Get Ohn (Fairlight Mix)' swerves down a side street into a footwurkin' face-off by sliding to a mutilated mix of Jon E Cash and Chez Damier played underwater. Next we hit the erogenous interzone of 'Maze' and that incapacitatingly lush bassline designed to lock into your central nervous system and send shockwaves of piloerection to every fucking corner of your soul.

After that, we're cynically dumped into the Ferraro-esque Prince tribute 'Purple Splazsh', and on into the Detroit ghetto stalk of 'Let's Fly'. The dissonant robo-crunk of 'The Kettle Men' and closing entry 'Casanova' confirm that if anything, Actress only suffers from a surfeit of ideas. Proof, if it were needed, that there is a sprawling future beyond the stasis of so much contemporary electronic music.
items._genre: experimental electronic / IDM / bass music / ambient
items._cn_summary: Actress在2008年凭《Hazyville》奠定地位后，将目光投向未知领域，在更短时间内完成这张专辑，呈现出碎片化却对称的结构。评论重点提及多首曲目：'Futureproofing'以密封气闸的压迫感开场，'Always Human'早已广为流传，'Get Ohn (Fairlight Mix)'将dancehall制作人Jon E Cash与底特律deep house代表Chez Damier的素材以水下混音方式拼贴，'Maze'的低频线条被形容为直击中枢神经。'Purple Splazsh'带有John Ferraro式的Prince致敬意味，'Let's Fly'呈现底特律街头潜行感，'The Kettle Men'与终曲'Casanova'则走向失谐的机器人crunk节拍。整张专辑刻意抵抗任何分类标签，问题在于想法过于丰沛而非匮乏，为停滞的当代电子音乐提供了一种蔓延向未来的可能路径。

items.excerpt: Nairobi, Kenya’s KMRU debuts on Mego with a suite of serene ambient scenes after emerging with Four Tet-like electronica releases in 2019 and recently starring on ‘Alternate African Reality - Electronic, Electroacoustic And Experimental Music From Africa And The Diaspora’ Known as Joseph Kamaru to his pals, KMRU was hailed by RA as one of ’15 East African Artists You Need To Hear’ in 2018 and is a regular performer at Nyege Nyege Festival in Uganda, beside... more
items.body:
Nairobi, Kenya’s KMRU debuts on Mego with a suite of serene ambient scenes after emerging with Four Tet-like electronica releases in 2019 and recently starring on ‘Alternate African Reality - Electronic, Electroacoustic And Experimental Music From Africa And The Diaspora’

Known as Joseph Kamaru to his pals, KMRU was hailed by RA as one of ’15 East African Artists You Need To Hear’ in 2018 and is a regular performer at Nyege Nyege Festival in Uganda, beside performing at CTM and Gamma Festival. For his Mego release ‘Peel’ it appears he’s been listening to label hero Fennesz, the Austrian experimental guitarist, or Will Long aka Celer, with whom his tracks share a certain, longing melancholy in their long, sighing arrangements of glistening and creaking ambient pads and mournful post-rock/cienmatic elegance. 

“The subtle calming atmosphere within Peel belies the compositional prowess as layers of delicate sounds wrap around each other creating a hybrid new form ambient musics both captivating through it’s textural depth and kaleidoscopic patterns. The track titles lend themselves to the themes and mood set within: Why are you here, Well, Solace, Klang, Insubstantial and the title track. This is a deep heartfelt journey with a new strong voice being expressed through the means of organically presented electronic ambient sounds, one which reveals further layers on repeat listens.”
items._cn_summary: 来自肯尼亚内罗毕的KMRU在奥地利实验厂牌Mego发行首张全长专辑《Peel》，从早期偏Four Tet式的电子舞曲转向沉稳内省的氛围音乐创作。整张专辑以绵长的呼吸式编排展开，闪烁着微光的环境音垫与细微的摩擦声交织，呈现出哀婉而克制的忧郁气质，与Fennesz及Celer的作品存在精神上的亲缘性。评论指出，表面的宁静氛围之下隐藏着精心的层次组织——细碎的声响彼此环绕缠绕，形成兼具织体深度与万花筒式纹样变化的新型环境音乐形态。曲目名称如《Why are you here》《Solace》《Klang》等直接映射作品所探讨的主题与情绪。这是一段深沉而诚挚的心路旅程，以有机感十足的电子环境声响传达出一种尚未被充分认识的新声音，值得反复聆听以揭示其中更深的层次。

items.body:
Sferic/Faitiche emissary Roméo Poirier pairs up with stylistic mentor Jan Jelinek on a sampler's delight, answering Jelinek's romantic 2005 gem 'Collage of Digital Passion' with a montaged mirror image that fizzes with plunderphonic warmth.

Jelinek has been using The Exposures pseudonym since 2003, most notably pillaging micro-samples from numerous R&B records on "Collage Of Digital Passion” issued by Prefuse 73’s Eastern Developments label back in 2005. In his by-now inimitable loop-finding style, that track has become a bit of a low-slung classic, reminding us not only of his iconic productions of the early 2000’s, but also of Anthony Shakir’s iconic ‘Mr. Shakir's Beat Store’ from just a couple of years earlier.

For his “version”, Poirier flips “I hate you!" samples with fanciful, theatrical soundscapes that ooze warmth, capturing the essence of Jelinek's original perfectly.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是采样艺术家 Roméo Poirier 与风格导师 Jan Jelinek 合作的作品，后者以 The Exposures 化名活动，擅长从大量 R&B 唱片中挖掘微小采样片段并进行拼贴。作品被描述为对 Jelinek 2005 年名曲的一次镜像回应，延续了他标志性的循环挖掘手法，将偷取来的素材与温暖、带有戏剧性的声景融合。Poirier 在自己的版本中翻转了"I hate you!"采样，制造出洋溢着温度的拼贴质感，精准捕捉了原作精神。整体听感介于 Plunderphonic 拼贴美学与实验电子之间，评论将其与 Anthony Shakir 的经典采样作品并列讨论，属于独立/地下厂牌发行的实验性小众作品，对偏好微观采样和声音拼贴的听众具有相当吸引力。

items.body:
Krautrock’s longhair godfathers flocked to a Berlin lake in 2018, playing rarely heard fan faves such as ‘Why Don’t You Eat Carrots?’, accompanied by the Richardchor Neukolln choir, and captured - crowd noise included - on digital recorder for posterity. Trust they still know how to veer from rocking swag to wild-eyed noise like few others...

“August 4 2018 in the scorching Berlin sunshine, Faust performed a truly stunning and unique set, featuring iconic material rarely, if ever, performed live. What made this so special was hearing such pieces as “Why Don’t You Eat Carrots?” played live, with the small choir perfecting that part of the song. For those lucky enough to have been there, they witnessed a Faust show never seen before, or ever to be repeated.

This CD was recorded on a professional digital recorder (not a phone!!!). It has been lovingly remastered by Amaury Cambuzat, possibly the only person capable of doing so, without compromising the nature of the show. Nothing has been added, so there will be imperfections. It comes packaged in a mini LP gatefold wallet, with a gloss spot varnish.”
items._cn_summary: 2018年柏林湖畔音乐节现场录音，德国实验摇滚先驱Faust携Neukölln合唱团登台，演绎极少公开表演的曲目，包括《Why Don'T You Eat Carrots?》等人声配合段落。专辑由专业数字录音设备完整收录现场环境音，由Amaury Cambuzat操刀重制，刻意保留演出中的瑕疵与即兴瞬间，不做后期干预。从摇滚律动到狂暴噪音的极端切换贯穿整场，Faust招牌式的不可预测结构在户外场地获得新的空间感与声学维度。包装采用迷你黑胶对折样式还原实体质感。整体作为历史性演出存档，对Krautrock研究与实验音乐场景而言具有文献价值，录音方式忠实呈现了现场不可复制的一次性事件。

items.body:
Bonkers plunderphonic cut-up of Heiner Goebbels & Alfred Harth’s sampled rendition of 1960’s Revolutionary Pekinese Opera from China, helmed by experimental force of nature Otomo Yoshihide on turntables & guitar.

“With the blessing of OTOMO himself, one of the cornerstones of nineties avant-garde officially returns to vinyl. A melting pot of musicians, sounds, and experimentation, all masterminded by the Deus Ex Machina of Fukushima. These compositions haven’t lost a single shred of their original allure, striking us today with the same raw power and innovative drive of thirty years ago, when they first burst onto the global avant-garde scene.”
items._genre: plunderphonics / avant-garde / experimental / turntablism / world fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由日本实验音乐核心人物Otomo Yoshihide操刀，对Heiner Goebbels与Alfred Harth于1960年代改编自中国革命京剧的采样作品进行了彻底的拼贴重构。Otomo Yoshihide本人给予授权，使得九十年代前卫场景的重要拼贴作品得以黑胶再版。他以唱机与吉他为核心手段，对原始的中国京剧采样素材进行拆解与重组，将六十年代的政治声音档案、九十年代的avant-garde实验态度以及东方的戏曲传统熔于一炉。整张作品保持了三十年前首度问世时的原始冲击力与创新能量，将不同文化语境下的声音碎片转化为新的听觉结构，展现了拼贴艺术跨越时空的持续生命力。

Building on a decade of work spanning cuts for Brownswood thru to jams with Matthew Herbert and Matt Davies, ‘Arc’ finds Yorkshire-bred artist Barley fully indulge... more
items.body:
On Kirk Barley’s definitive solo gem, alternative tunings and a tactile feel for pitching rhythms generate their gentlest and most absorbing work, twinkling amid a microcosm of similar, exploratory productions from Mark Fell & Rian Treanor thru to Aleksi Perälä, Beatrice Dillon, Terry Riley & Jon Hassell.

Building on a decade of work spanning cuts for Brownswood thru to jams with Matthew Herbert and Matt Davies, ‘Arc’ finds Yorkshire-bred artist Barley fully indulge formative passions for microtonal just intonation - as seeded in Terry Riley’s ‘Shri Camel’ - and slippery syncopation to the fullest. Half solo, proper, and half peppered with percussion by regular spar, Matt Davies, it follows his nose for open frontiers of alternative tunings and wonky meter with the blend of low key modesty and prism-pushing tekkerz that have long endeared his work to lovers of lower case experimental music. 

Sweetly balanced between timeless, folk-soul-wise and futurist sensibilities, the half hour suite knits hyaline synths and rippling gamelan metallophonics with clarinet and guitar in lissom, sloshing shapes that effortlessly seduce, rather than demand, the listener’s attention. In particular we are drawn to the bits in duo with Davies, floating sublime ideas in the dreamlike, inverted dub architexture of ‘Ion’, settling on mind like a strangely bucolic Incus work on ’Sundry’, and thru the exquisite, tip-toed rhythms of ‘Ecstatic’, to a trippier, bittersweet type of ante-chamber music on ‘Fret (Hear)’.

He’s also deeply charming when left to his own devices. Ambient opener ‘Billow’ calls to mind the tenderness of Cotton Goods works, and ‘Knead’ chases a certain geist of Irdial or Plaid-esque gamelantronica into the sublime title tune, while ‘Prism’ most beautifully ties all his interests in a melting dream sequence which he caps with the harmonic nightlight glow of ‘Column’.
items._cn_summary: Kirk Barley的专辑《Arc》建立在过去十年的创作积累之上，将微音律与替代调律体系作为核心方法论，融合加美兰金属质感合成器、单簧管与吉他，形成透明流动的声音纹理。整张专辑半小时左右，分为独奏段落与与打击乐手Matt Davies合作的对话片段，节奏处理上偏向柔和的非同步律动而非强硬驱动。制作手法上兼具民间根源的温暖质感与未来主义音色探索，多首曲目呈现出低限实验音乐的克制美学，以催眠式的渐变而非戏剧化对比推动聆听体验。在Boomkat这类注重前沿实验的独立平台上获得详尽推介，文章对该专辑在低调实验音乐谱系中的定位进行了充分阐述，乐评内容充实且具有明确的艺术价值判断。

items.body:
Jazzy 1977 rework of a traditional Japanese wedding song, backed with Visible Cloaks’ weightless ambient electronic remix

The 1977 version was conceived by Jazz man Jun Arasaki and his group Nine Sheep, and executed in one take (this recording) on five sanshin, four winds, piano, bass, percussion and drums for a TV broadcast. It’s somehow solemn yet joyous in a slow and stately way, with lyrics describing how “beautiful buds unfold”.

Fourth World inhabitants and dreamers Visible Cloaks remix ‘Kajyadhi Fu Bushi’ in their own image, resulting a diaphanous, gauzy swell of harmonised synth chorales infiltrated by playful ghosts in the machine and weft with elusive traces of the original vocal to sound like a Google deep dream reverie of the real thing.
items._genre: experimental / ambient electronic / Japanese traditional / jazz fusion
items._cn_summary: 这是一张融合日本传统婚庆歌曲与现代实验电子的跨界作品。原版录制于1977年，由爵士乐手荒崎纯与Nine Sheep乐队采用五把三线、四支管乐器、钢琴、贝斯与鼓等编制，在一次录制中完成电视广播演出，风格庄严而缓慢欢快，歌词描绘花蕾绽放之美。Visible Cloaks的混音版本则将原作转化为透明朦胧的合成器合唱浪潮，机器中潜伏的灵动幽灵与原作人声的若隐若现痕迹交织，营造出如深度梦境般的幻听体验。整张作品在传统器乐、即兴爵士与环境电子之间建立对话，既保留了原曲的文化根基，又通过电子手法重构出全新的听觉空间，展现了跨时代、跨风格的声音实验思路。

Reflecting the stress and strain of the modern interconnected world, Higuchi controls the chaos on... more
items.body:
Takahide Higuchi searches for light in the darkness on their follow-up to 2023's 'uchigawa tankentai' EP, a surprisingly personal collection of mutant children's songs and playground rhymes that Higuchi subverts with chipmunked voices, cartoonish samples, Mark Fell-like FM synths and rhythms inspired by Brazilian funk, footwork and ghetto house.

Reflecting the stress and strain of the modern interconnected world, Higuchi controls the chaos on 'HIKARIGASASHIKOMU', appearing straight out of the gate with a chorus of corrupted voices that are pitched into alien screams, paired with shrill digital stabs and ketmized FX. It's disorienting stuff, far more eccentric than the MIDI-jazz-footwork echoes that characterized 2021's 'Yasuragi Land'. Here, Higuchi appears to be turning their distant childhood memories into demonic ghost chants and hypnogogic club inversions: nursery rhymes that have been chopped to shreds and spliced with hiccuping beats. 

'Omoi' is like SND making footwork, while lead single 'Hard Reclining' is a seemingly mismatched fusion of folk-y vocal chants, vintage R&B guitars licks and flimsy city pop drums. Then on 'Horomiro', after being blasted by squelchy acid sequences, we're hit with a barrage of cartoonish samples: woody hits, repurposed gliding squares, transformer scratches and chaotic vocals. It's almost too much, standing in stark contrast to Higuchi's relatively spare early work. But thematically it's on point; Higuchi wants us to live in his world for a moment or two, experiencing his internal world so we can get a better handle on his psychedelic sound.
items._genre: experimental electronic / footwork / glitch / IDM / mutant pop
items._cn_summary: Foodman（Takahide Higuchi）在专辑《HIKARIGASASHIKOMU》中延续其变异童谣路线，将童年记忆中的儿歌与操场韵律解构为异化的电子声响。制作中大量使用变调人声、卡通采样、尖锐数字刺响与酸性合成器序列，节奏根基来自巴西funk、芝加哥footwork与ghetto house。相较前作《Yasuragi Land》的MIDI爵士气质，此作更为混乱与不安，呼应现代互联世界的压迫感。曲目如《Omoi》呈现SND式footwork框架，《Hard Reclining》将民谣人声、老式R&B吉他与city pop鼓机并置，《Horomiro》则以酸性序列轰炸配合密集卡通碎片。整体创作将私人情感投射为催眠俱乐部式的倒错影像，在极繁的拼贴中构建出独属作者内心的迷幻声景。

items.body:
For new initiates and avant-garde fiends alike, this Xenakis collection renders a breathtaking survey of works by the radical composer, theorist, architect and engineer, spanning the period 1956-1974 and featuring some of the greatest works of the 20th century, including the awe-inspiring sonic architecture of ‘Persepolis’.

Inarguably one of the most important composers to blend electronic process and classical orchestration, Greek-French artist Iannis Xenakis made an indelible impression on the 20th century with his staggeringly complex feats of musical engineering. Regularly cited as an influence by composers ranging from Florian Hecker thru Autechre and Reinhold Friedl, Xenakis’s polymath pursuits in hybridising music, architecture and mathematics generated a bewildering array of sounds and structures which have rarely, if ever, been bettered in terms of their sheer scope, scale and technical ingenuity.

It’s possible to break down Xenakis’ approach to composition, and its results, as an extension of his experiences in armed combat, fighting for Greece’s left wing liberationists against the German army and later the British during WWII, with the latter leaving him blinded in one eye. He would eventually leave Greece in 1947 after graduating university with a degree in civil engineering, and before he could be conscripted into the Greek army, who didn’t look favourably on left wing sympathisers. Moving from Greece to Paris left him with a sense of guilt at betraying his friends, and a sense that “I had to do something important to regain the right to live. It wasn’t just a question of music - it was something much more significant.” 

That significant something turned out to be a mind-blowing, multi-disciplinary oeuvre practically unprecedented in the history of music, architecture and art; a radical synthesis of ideas which embraced new technology and abstraction as a means to realise and create a new world in the aftermath of WWII. Like the Italian futurists before him, Xenakis would draw on the chaotic soundfield of war, and combined with a strong knowledge of experimental classical music and a special nous of maths, Xenakis’ subsequent studies with Olivier Messiaen and work with Parisian architect Le Corbusier would prompt him to composing groundbreaking new music during the 1950s.

This 2CD contains works from that era, stretching right back to the pranging clangour and jet-like eruptions of Achorripsis [1956-57], an early example of his stochastic style of composition, thru the dizzying, chronic dynamics of Syrmos [1959], and to some of the earliest work composed by a computer, the 7090 IBM, in ST/48(St/48-1,240162).

But it’s Xenakis’ ’60s/‘70s work where his genius is mst evident, from the breathtaking scope of Polytope De Montréal [1967] - written for four orchestras in the same space in the French Pavilion at Expo ’67 - to the gobsmacking dimensions of his seminal Persépolis [1971], which was realised for the Shah of Iran, plus the frankly terrifying, computerised wormhole of Polytope De Cluny [1972-74].

We can’t reasonably describe this set as anything other than indispensable for fans of electronic music from its inception to the modern day.
items._genre: experimental / avant-garde / contemporary classical / electronic / stochastic
items._cn_summary: 这套双碟合辑收录了希腊裔法国作曲家Iannis Xenakis从1956到1974年间的代表性作品，涵盖其随机音乐（stochastic music）风格的早期探索到晚期的空间音响建筑创作。从早期作品Achorripsis的尖锐碰撞声响，到用IBM 7090计算机创作的ST/48——音乐史上最早的计算机辅助作曲之一——再到为蒙特利尔世博会法国馆设计的Polytope De Montréal以及为伊朗国王实现的Persépolis，作品展现了作曲家将数学理论、建筑思维与音乐结构融合的独特方法论。Xenakis将二战战场上的混乱声场转化为抽象的声学语言，结合与Le Corbusier合作的经验，发展出前所未有的多学科创作体系。这套选辑对其长达近二十年的创作脉络提供了较为完整的鸟瞰式呈现。

items.excerpt: A decade since debuting as Ndagga Rhythm Force, Mark Ernestus’ incredible band draw on 100’s of hours studio and live practice for a staggering new suite of Senegalese x Berlin-styled mbalax steppers that prove, where needed, why they’re one of the best to do it right now. items.body:
A decade since debuting as Ndagga Rhythm Force, Mark Ernestus’ incredible band draw on 100’s of hours studio and live practice for a staggering new suite of Senegalese x Berlin-styled mbalax steppers that prove, where needed, why they’re one of the best to do it right now. Absolutely exemplary, transcendent music for those that know.

Back at the start of the 2010s dub techno pioneer Mark Ernestus was spending a lot of time in Senegal, immersing in styles and patterns that historically underlined the reggae and dub musics he would heavily reference in his pivotal records made as Maurizio/Basic Channel/Rhythm & Sound, as co-produced with Moritz Von Oswald during the ‘90s and into the ’00s. 

In the process of researching and getting down to the roots of his passions, Ernestus encountered some of Senegal’s top tier musicians and recorded the Jeri-Jeri ensemble, revolving vocalist Mbene Diatta Seck and sabar drummer Bada Seck, and generating in 2013 the ‘800% Ndagga’ CD and its ’Ndagga Versions’ sibling, which better showcased Ernestus’ famed dub tekkerz inseparably woven into Senegalese music and the roots of myriad Afro-diasporic sounds.

That unit would morph into Ndagga Rhythm Force, producing an LP and trio of 12”s in 2015-2016 that set them on course to become one of the most impressive African bands on the contemporary gig circuit, throwing down live sets known to effortlessly go over 2 hours and propel so many legs and minds to new shapes and feels - trust they slay every time and should be top of all must-see lists.

With ‘Khadim’ Ndagga ditch their guitars and recalibrate a more lissom trio of voice and acoustic instruments bound with Ernestus’ Prophet 5 synth - the same model he’s relied upon since the Basic Channel days - on four extended songs that allow more light, space and emotion into a signature, rolling sound, centre-staging Mbene Seck’s husky diva croon over Bada Seck and Serigne Mamoune Seck’s dual, polymetric percussion, and judiciously juggled with Ernestus’ anti-gravity basses and plangent dub chord syncopation. 

In traditionally open-ended frameworks the quartet take all the time needed to stretch out and wrap heads into the tapestries of their storytelling grooves. A newfound atmospheric pressure and presence emerges in procession from the location recordings that fringe ‘Lamp Fall’ and its ode to a local mosque, reverberating in acres of implied space set by the ricocheting sabar drums and near-infrasonic subs, thru to the devotional depths of ’Nimzat’, rippling with thunderous chords and doleful ache. 

At its core are the LP’s most impressive parts; ‘Dieuw Bakhul’ uncoils a spellbinding Wolof tale of treachery to the rafters amid tempestuous chords that writhe stereo-wide with red-lining bite whilst drums knot sinuous, serpentine, to be resolved in the breathtaking 13’ steppers’ flight of ‘Khadim’, which lyrically hails Islam’s role in guiding Senegal to postcolonial times, spiritually meditates on bluest minor key riffs, and physically elevates bodies with aerodynamic finesse and hypnotic chronics kin to the best reggae and its offshoots. 

Deadly, soul and hoof gripping tunes. Do not miss!
items._genre: mbalax / dub / Senegalese percussion / electronic fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Mark Ernestus与Ndagga Rhythm Force乐队的第三张正式作品，从上一张以吉他为主导的编制转变为更精简的三重奏结构——人声、塞内加尔传统打击乐与Ernestus标志性的Prophet 5合成器。乐队放弃了吉他音色，留出更多空间让Seck家族成员的多节奏鼓组与人声领唱展开叙事。四首长篇曲目采用开放式框架，鼓手们在传统节奏模式中展开长时间的拉伸与变奏，合成器则提供低音线条与dub式和弦切分。录音部分在塞内加尔实地完成，空间感与声场层次被刻意放大，营造出仪式感的氛围。整体制作将柏林dub techno的制作美学与塞内加尔mbalax传统深度交织，形成一种跨国界的混合音乐语言，延续了Ernestus从Basic Channel时期以来对非洲离散音乐根源的探索脉络。

items.body:
Mika Vainio & Ilpo Väisänen’s first ever release as Panasonic, originally issued in 1994 as the "Panasonic EP", a while before they were forced by the electronic goods coroporation of the same name to drop the A...

A real slice of history right here, presenting longer and harder versions of a cut that appeared in a shorter form on Mika’s Ø album ‘Metri’, co-credited to him and Ilpo, and here going longer and doubled up with another duo battering ram, ‘Murtaja’. Both tunes sound very much of their time, when European techno was forged tougher to demand, paralleling movements of harder Chicago house and Detroit warehouse techno.

In Panasonic’s case, the results were typically ascetic, mostly bleached of discernible melody beyond rhythmelodic cadence, and locked, bloody-minded, to icy tattoos that reflected their origins in Finnish warehouse parties, and would pin them on the international techno and electronic music maps. Trust that ‘Muuntaja’ still leaves welts from its distorted kicks, and contains subs primed to quake foundations, whilst the B-side is ideal for gnashing rave punks and bass drum fetishists.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了芬兰双人组Panasonic（Mika Vainio与Ilpo Väisänen）1994年首张发行物的再版，将原始EP中的两首曲目以更长、更暴力的形式呈现。'Muuntaja'保留了扭曲的低频冲击与足以撼动地基的次低频，节奏如烙印般冷酷精准；B面的'Murtaja'则面向偏爱底鼓打击与锐利rave质感的听众。整体声响极为克制，几乎剥离了旋律，仅保留节奏与音色的硬核骨架，反映了上世纪九十年代中叶芬兰仓库派对的严酷美学，也与同期芝加哥硬派house和底特律仓库techno形成平行对话。作为芬兰地下电子场景的早期文献，此作确立了二人在国际techno与电子音乐版图上的坐标。

items.body:
A spiritual session of seminal nyabinghi grounation from Dadawah circa 1974, perhaps the most mind-expanding, important spiritual dub reissue we've heard this last couple of decades and inarguably a template of sorts for the whole burial mix aesthetic. It doesn't get much more influential, or spiritual, than this one.

Dadawah were led by Ras Michael, guiding a traditional set up of nyabinghi (ceremonial Rasta drums), bass, guitar, brass and Piano organ in four extended excursions over sublime, psychedelic terrain in a mode that sounds uncannily like a precursor to Rhythm & Sound's 'Making History' from decades later.

As with much of the best material from the era, much of the magic was elicited and embellished in post production, with Lloyd Charmers and Federal engineer George Raymond apparently staying up all night after the session to mix the recording, imbuing the tracks with a dazed, wide-open and echoing personal space.

Keeping the standards impeccably high, the album was lovingly restored at Abbey Road and comes housed in heavy stock, hand assembled card sleeves, looking every bit the classic that it is.
items._genre: nyabinghi dub / spiritual dub / roots reggae / world music
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年左右的专辑由Ras Michael领导的Dadawah乐队录制，以传统拉斯塔法里教仪式鼓乐为核心，融合贝斯、吉他、铜管与钢琴风琴，在四首长篇幅曲目中展开冥想式的迷幻声景。制作人Lloyd Charmers与工程师George Raymond在录音结束后通宵混音，将现场素材转化为回声深邃、声场开阔的空间化效果，成为日后dub美学与burial mix风格的源头之一。评论将其与Rhythm & Sound的《Making History》相提并论，指出两者在极简化、低频律动与精神性氛围上的传承关系。专辑由Abbey Road进行母带重制，厚卡纸手工封面还原了原始质感。这是一张将宗教仪式、非洲节奏传统与dub混音技术熔于一炉的作品，对后世电子音乐与ambient场景中的空间感塑造有深远影响。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the more unusual progressive bands to emerge from the 1970s boom in the Netherlands, HETPANDORRA ENSEMBLE existed from 1973 until 1980 and left one album in its wake and very little infoabout its existence with nobody even sure of where the band was formed exactly. This band that wasled by guitarist Dolf Planteijdt who eschewed the symphonic prog tendencies of fellow Dutch actslike Focus or even more pop-fueled vocal acts like Earth & Fire but rather the band featured abizarre mishmash of heavy King Crimson guitar angst, Mahavishnu Orchestra inspired jazz fusion andextreme free improvisation liberties with varying musical motifs suddenly shifting midstream intosomething completely different. In addition to the more contemporary prog references, this band wasalso smitten with the abstract modern classical styles of George Crumb as well as impressionistssuch as Ravel and Bartok's Eastern European folklore works.The ENSEMBLE's entire presentation itself was a little odd with this act featuring only five membersand releasing a single album ironically titled III in 1978. What makes it even weirder is that thecover looks like a Patti Smith reject which honestly conveys absolutely nothing about the musicinside. No wonder this talented band was overlooked and lost to the annals of time! The lineup onIII features the cast members of Planteijdt (guitars), Dolf Planteijdt (guitars), Roland Brunt(flute), Gert-Jan Blom (bass) and Wilfred Snellens who replaced the recently deceased Jean Eble. Thealbum was released on the Disaster Electronics label and originally featured five tracks however the2012 Modulus reissue adds an extra seven bonus tracks of unreleased material.For all its eclecticism, HET PANDORRA ENSEMBLE was primarily steeped in complex jazz fusion motifsthat incorporated angular avant-prog complexities and King Crimson's "Red" as a template for gnarledguitar tones. The album displays a fairly interesting balance between skronky dissonance and morecleverly constructed melodic touches implementing everything from moments of space rock to Spanishflamenco. Three tracks "Door Mekaar," "Kanon Pittoresk" and "Karotten" all extend past the 10-minuteplaying time while the remaining two are much shorter clocking in under 5. "Kanon Pittoresk" is theperfect example of this band's extremities meandering from super chill to ridiculously sped uptempos and sizzling guitar soloing with a rather Latin-inspired bass groove. The band's album iscompletely instrumental with no vocals except a very a single moment of wordless chanting."Door Mekaar" showcases a reimagined King Crimson take on jazz fusion with twin guitar attacks andover-the-top complex arrangements while "Kanon Pittoresk" is more of a wild free-for-all that deftlyblends angular avant-prog fusion with more melodic rock hybridizations. The short track "Ritme 7000"serves only as a palette cleanser. It has sort of a medieval folk feel but only distantly. "Drei"takes a complete 180 and introduces a chamber rock style with a lengthy shrill monotone that slowlygenerates a creepy mood setting that pretty much stays in droning mode for 4 1/2 minutes with only afew surprise vocal chants and occasional tinkling of random sounds. "Karotten" ends the album withcontinues the detached eeriness of its predecessor and slowly transmogrifies into a guitar drivenseries of KC inspired works that evolve into a more fiery example of jazz fusion thus taking thealbum full circle. HET PANDORRA ENSEMBLE was sort of the fish out of water and even though it joined the ranks of theprog universe late in the game still retained that fiery experimental passion that exploded in thelate 1960s and became somewhat commercialized by 1973. III is a rather unpredictable slice of Dutchprog that sounds like no other. A second album was in the works but never came to fruition leaving aslew of musical carcasses to gather dust on the shelves for many decades before finally emerging asa whopping double album reissue in 2012. While the album could use some fine-tuning to make it morecohesive and sometimes feels extremely disjointed, for those with an appetite for wild untamedartistry run amok then this one will prove quite satisfying.
items._cn_summary: 这是荷兰小厂牌Disaster Electronics于1978年发行的唯一专辑，由五人乐团Het Pandorra Ensemble录制。吉他手Dolf Planteijdt领衔，乐团将King Crimson式扭曲吉他棱角、Mahavishnu Orchestra启发的爵士融合骨架，以及George Crumb、Ravel、Bartók等抽象现代古典语汇熔于一炉。全器乐编制在十至二十分钟的长篇曲目中频繁切换速度与动机，从超松弛段落骤然转入灼热吉他独奏与拉丁律动贝斯线。《Door Mekaar》展示双吉他交织的复杂安排，《Kanon Pittoresk》则是棱角分明的前卫融合与旋律摇滚杂交的自由战场。《Ritme 7000》仅作过渡，提供淡淡中世纪民谣气息。2012年Modulus再版增补七首未发行曲目，扩展了这批几乎被遗忘的荷兰实验遗产的可见度。

items.album: Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari
items.artist: Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy
items.excerpt:
Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release,
Under an Endless Sky
.
In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari,
Songs of Compassion
is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics.
Francesco Paolo Paladi
items.body: Known for playing with County Joe McDonald, and for her experimental sound band The United States of America, Dorothy Moskowitz came back in 2023 with United States of Alchemy and their well-received release, Under an Endless Sky . In collaboration with avant-garde composer and filmmaker Francesco Paolo Paladino, and poet and music writer Luca Chino Ferrari, Songs of Compassion is eleven songs containing subversive and at times beautiful music, and richly evocative lyrics. Francesco Paolo Paladino and Luca Chino Ferrari | Photo by Maria Assunta Karini Songs of Compassion has two challenges for the listener. The first is the music, called variously avant-garde, ambient, modal, non-linear, and a few more. It is played mostly on pianos mixed in and out of the foreground, sometimes doubled, and sometimes out of phase, joined by strings, woodwinds, synth washes, and steely sounds. Initially disorienting, the music serves to remind us how locked our minds are to Western notions of harmonic movement. It speaks of alternative musical narratives much older and much further away. They are songs that subvert the song: more like Steve Reich than Steve Stills; more like Phillip Glass than Phil Collins. UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY - Pale Wanderer At the same time, there are the poetic yet strikingly contemporary lyrics. �Pale Wanderer� talks about the fact that authoritarianism needs willing accomplices, describing what happens �When you make a deal with darkness.� UNITED STATES OF ALCHEMY (Dorothy Moskowitz, Francesco Paolo Paladino e Luka Chino Ferrari) by Silentes �Charlottesville� (written with the late Joe Byrd) evokes the time not long ago when torch-wielding nazis, proud of the metaphoric Ns on their tunics, chanted the antisemitic tropes paraphrased in Moskowitz�s words, �We�ll be one people, pure of race/No greedy throng could take our place� . Besides the overtly political lyrics, in the tradition of 1960s protest songs, there are also thoughtful meditations on mortality and our place in the universe. The message is high-minded yet sincere and direct. World weary and wise, Moskowitz�s voice inhabits the evocative philosophical lyrics with the authority of a skilled method actor. The melodies unfold like streams of consciousness, rising and falling, not following expected diatonic chord progressions, but honouring, instead, the value of each word. Moskowitz�s piano acts as another voice and sometimes a kind of Greek chorus commenting on the proceedings. The surrounding music frames, creates pulses and dissonances, and shimmers. The return of Dorothy Moskowitz with her renamed project has arrived in a moment quite similar to the times that spawned its predecessor. Political division, unrest, and uncertainty always generate artistic reaction, and United States of Alchemy roared back to life with their epic 24-minute opening track �Under an Endless Sky� in 2023, serving perhaps as an �In-A-Gadda-Da-Vida� for our times. Songs of Compassion continues to challenge how we think about our world. It�s music that defies the song form, while doing exactly what music is supposed to do�enrich the human condition. Find the artist online. The title track from the 2023 U.S. of Alchemy recording Under an Endless Sky by Dorothy Moskowitz & United States of Alchemy Further reading Cris Derksen - The Visit (Review) Tiny Sun - Vanishment (Review) Maria Ka - Di Mashin (Review) Further listening You will find a number of Dorothy Moskowitz's works on Race The Sky , most recently on Podgrammes #022 and #019.
items.label: Songs of Compassion
items._cn_summary: Dorothy Moskowitz 与作曲家 Francesco Paolo Paladino 及诗人 Luca Chino Ferrari 合作，推出专辑《Songs of Compassion》，收录十一首歌曲。音乐以钢琴为主角，辅以弦乐、木管、合成器音色和金属质感声响，通过相位偏移、双轨叠加等手法构建非线性结构，挑战听众对西方和声进行的固有认知。歌词延续1960年代抗议歌曲传统，《Pale Wanderer》剖析极权主义的合谋机制，《Charlottesville》与已故 Joe Byrd 合作，直接引用新纳粹口号加以讽喻，同时融入对死亡与人类在宇宙中位置的哲思。Moskowitz 的演唱方式自由展开旋律走向，不依赖传统调性进行，钢琴演奏如希腊歌队般参与叙事。整张专辑将极端政治批判与哲学冥想融于一体，音乐与文字形成多层互文。评论文章末尾截断，但已充分展示作品在政治深度与音乐实验性方面的双重野心。
