items.body: Zurich, Switzerland industrial metal act Susurration released the EP “Dominance” in mid-July 2026, the first half of a double EP that pairs with a companion EP titled “Submission” due later. The release is self-released and arrives ahead of Susurration’s forthcoming full-length album, “Trauma Ties”. “Dominance” is available to stream on Spotify. The EP builds directly on the band’s 2024 debut album “Hate Is My Love Language”, pushing further into aggressive EBM (electronic body music) textures layered against distorted guitars. The lineup behind “Dominance” is vocalist Jessy Bäsecke-Beltrametti, drummer Dave Wieser, keyboardist Hannes Bachofner and guitarist Michael Hirst. The lead track, “Consensual Noise Content”, opens on stripped-back dark electro before shifting into a heavier metal passage with blast-beat drumming. The video single “Break Me Down” carries a driving, percussion-led arrangement, and a remix of the track “Boibitch” adds additional industrial metal weight aimed at dancefloor tempos. The EP also includes remix contributions from Anna Soares and Dunkelsucht. A full tracklist beyond these confirmed songs has not been published. “Dominance” centers themes of self-determined identity, control and vulnerability. Susurration has described representation as a core goal of the band: “For us this kind of representation and inclusion is one of the main goals of susurration,” the band has stated, referring to its identity as a queer-feminist act led by a non-binary vocalist. Video for ‘Break Me Down’ Susurration released an official video for “Break Me Down”, directed by Jess Baumgartner. The video was shot around BDSM and fetish imagery, including candle wax and light bondage, and depicts submissive sexuality as a form of claimed power rather than shame. About Susurration Susurration began in 2010 in Zurich, Switzerland, as a solo project by songwriter and vocalist Jessy Bäsecke-Beltrametti, rooted in EBM and darkwave. Between 2022 and 2024, Susurration launched the single and video “Devotion To The Darkangel”, followed by the single “All Colors Are Black”, the single “Engels” and the single “Marks”. Around that period, Susurration transformed from a solo project into a full band, adding Dave Wieser on drums, Hannes Bachofner on keyboards, and Michael Hirst and Sabina Brunner on guitars. With this lineup, Susurration released its debut album “Hate Is My Love Language” in 2024, followed by a live premiere at Royal Baden in February 2025. The band draws on industrial, aggrotech, prog and black metal alongside its EBM foundation, and centers its output on themes of injustice, structural discrimination, queer identity and BDSM. “Dominance” continues that trajectory, pairing EBM electronics with heavier guitar work. The band has said the companion EP “Submission” will follow, ahead of the full-length album “Trauma Ties”.
items._cn_summary: 苏黎世乐队Susurration于2026年7月发行EP《Dominance》，为双EP计划的上半部分，下半部分《Submission》将于后续推出。作品延续了2024年首张专辑《Hate Is My Love Language》的方向，将EBM电子节拍与失真吉他、blast-beat鼓击并置，形成工业金属与暗电子的混合声响。主打曲《Consensual Noise Content》从精简的暗电子切入，转入金属段落；单曲《Break Me Down》以节奏驱动的打击乐结构为核心；另收录Anna Soares与Dunkelsucht的混音版本。EP主题围绕自主身份、控制与脆弱性展开，结合BDSM视觉叙事，将臣服描绘为一种主动获取的力量。乐队由非二元主唱Jessy Bäsecke-Beltrametti领导，明确以酷儿女性主义立场为核心创作动机。该EP为独立自发行作品，融合电子与重型乐器元素，但文章本质上为新闻稿性质的信息发布，缺乏深度乐评内容。

items.body: Italian darkwave band Christine Plays Viola released the standalone single “At Last, I Found You (Fear Increases Violent Emotions)” on 22 July 2026. The track closes out the story of the band’s 2026 album “F.I.V.E. (Fear Increases Violent Emotions)” and marks Christine Plays Viola’s first standalone release since that record. The song was written during the sessions for “F.I.V.E.” but held back from the album’s tracklist. Guitarist and bandleader Fabrizio Giampietro explained the decision: “At Last, I Found You was always the most immediate and instinctive song we wrote during the F.I.V.E. sessions. We deliberately left it off the album because we wanted listeners to experience that record’s emotional arc, without this song becoming its centre of gravity. Six months later, it felt like the right moment to finally share it.” The accompanying video is now available on YouTube. “At Last, I Found You” is out now on Bandcamp, Spotify and other digital platforms. At Last, I Found You (Fear Increases Violent Emotions) by Christine Plays Viola About Christine Plays Viola Christine Plays Viola formed in 2008 in Abruzzo, Italy, around an idea by guitarist Fabrizio Giampietro and drummer Daniele Palombizio, joined shortly after by bassist Desio Presutti and a singer known as Christian. The band released its debut album, “Innocent Awareness”, in 2011. In 2014 the group released “Vacua”, a record inspired by Spanish painter Francisco de Goya that anchored the band in the darkwave and new wave scene. Christine Plays Viola previously issued “Desolate Moments” as the third video single from “F.I.V.E.” in April 2026. The current lineup features Fabrizio Giampietro on guitars, synth and programming, Massimo Ciampani on vocals, Gianluca Orsini on drums and Marco Di Ianni on bass. “F.I.V.E. (Fear Increases Violent Emotions)”, the band’s fifth studio album, was released on 19 January 2026 via Cleopatra Records.
items._cn_summary: 意大利暗潮乐队Christine Plays Viola于2026年7月发布了单曲《At Last, I Found You》作为专辑《F.I.V.E.》的尾声式延伸。这首歌在专辑录制期间创作，但乐队刻意将其从正式曲目中排除，以保留专辑的情感弧线完整性，半年后才以独立单曲形式释出。乐队自2008年成立于意大利阿布鲁佐大区，由吉他手Fabrizio Giampietro和鼓手Daniele Palombizio创立，2014年凭借受西班牙画家戈雅启发的专辑《Vacua》确立了暗潮与新波风格定位。专辑《F.I.V.E.》于2026年1月通过埃及艳后唱片发行，是乐队的第五张录音室作品，延续了他们在暗潮、后朋克与新浪潮交汇区域的探索。

items.body: Swedish darkwave and synth artist EMMON’s track “Speak to Me (The Foreign Resort Remix)” is released on 24 July 2026 on Icons Creating Evil Art. The new version comes from Copenhagen post-punk and shoegaze trio The Foreign Resort and is the second remix to surface from EMMON’s upcoming remix album “ICONMIXED”, following an earlier version by Swiss-German duo SIIE. The Foreign Resort commented on reworking the track: “What do you do when the song you’re remixing already sounds amazing? You change it from electronic to analogue and add layers of reverb and distortion! And of course a Slayer-inspired guitar solo. Because it fits the song, and because we love metal!” “Speak to Me” was written by Emma Maria Nylén, André Winter and Anne-Marie Pappas, with lyrics by Emma Nylén. The remix can be pre-saved now via found.ee ahead of its release. About EMMON EMMON is the solo project of Swedish artist and producer Emma Nylén, conceived in 2001 as an art project while she was studying at Konstfack in Stockholm. She first gained recognition with the group Paris before continuing her musical path as EMMON, developing a sound that mixes EBM, synth-pop and darkwave with melodic, 1980s-referencing electronics. Her 2022 album “RECON” was followed by the 2024 EP “XCEPTION” and the album “ICON”, co-produced with Jimmy Monell. EMMON’s upcoming remix album “ICONMIXED” reworks tracks from her recent catalogue with contributions from acts including SIIE and The Foreign Resort. About The Foreign Resort The Foreign Resort formed in 2009 in Copenhagen, Denmark. The trio, made up of Mikkel Borbjerg Jakobsen on vocals, Steffan Petersen on bass and Morten Hansen on drums, has played more than 600 shows across North America and Europe, including SXSW, Iceland Airwaves, Cold Waves Festival, Wave Gotik Treffen and Amphi Festival. The band’s sound combines post-punk and shoegaze with a driving, dark production style.
items._cn_summary: 本文报道瑞典暗潮与合成器艺人EMMON的单曲Speak to Me发布由哥本哈根后朋克与自赏派三人组The Foreign Resort操刀的混音版本，属于其即将发行的混音专辑ICONMIXED的第二支单曲。The Foreign Resort的混音手法是将原本电子化的作品转化为模拟质感，加入混响、失真层次以及一段受Slayer启发的吉他独奏，体现了他们将后朋克、自赏派与金属元素融为一体的制作理念。EMMON作为Emma Nylén的个人项目，其原始作品融合EBM、合成器流行与暗潮，借鉴1980年代电子乐美学。The Foreign Resort则在600余场演出经验中形成了暗黑而驱动的后朋克与自赏派混合风格。整体内容为新单曲发布的事实性新闻稿，缺乏深度评论与乐评视角。

items.body: Berlin darkwave act Vlimmer has released the new single “Atemdauer“, backed with a German-language electronic interpretation of The Shins’ “Caring Is Creepy”. The single is out now on Bandcamp via Blackjack Illuminist Records. “Atemdauer” addresses acceptance and holding onto one’s identity against comparison and self-doubt. Musically, the track blends distorted post-punk bass, EBM rhythms and ominous synths with ethereal vocals, shifting into a hopeful, brief synth-pop coda toward the end. Atemdauer b/w Caring Is Creepy by Vlimmer About Vlimmer Vlimmer is the project of German musician, producer and label owner Alexander Leonard Donat, launched in 2015. The project built an extensive discography with an 18-part EP series released between 2015 and 2020, weaving together darkwave, post-punk, shoegaze and new wave with tribal drum patterns. Vlimmer’s debut album, “Nebenkörper”, followed in 2021, moving toward post-punk and adding industrial and noise-rock elements. The follow-up album, “Menschenleere”, arrived in 2022 with a more dancefloor-oriented sound, and the band’s third album, “Zerschöpfung“, was released in 2023. Donat also runs Blackjack Illuminist Records, the Berlin label that has released Vlimmer’s catalogue including “Atemdauer”.
items._cn_summary: Vlimmer 是柏林暗潮音乐人 Alexander Leonard Donat 的单人项目，新单曲「Atemdauer」探讨自我认同与自我怀疑的主题。音乐上融合了失真的后朋克贝斯、EBM 节奏、阴郁合成器与空灵人声，尾声转入一段短暂而明亮的合成器流行段落。B 面收录了对 The Shins「Caring Is Creepy」的德语电子改编。自 2015 年起，Vlimmer 通过 18 张 EP 系列积累了庞大曲目库，并在 2021 至 2023 年间发行了三张专辑，逐步从暗潮、后朋克与自赏派摇摆扩展到工业与舞曲化方向。整张单曲呈现成熟的类型融合手法，但整体仍属于暗潮/EBM 框架内的常规作品。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. Signal is mostly a very good album, with only a couple of songs that I feel are weaker than the rest.[I really think that if all bands looked at their albums as a single entity, rather than just a collection of individual songs, we could avoid the "filler syndrome"?the "gee, why don't we just toss this song on there?" mentality. A record's grooves should be considered sacred, deserving only of the very best work a band can create. Every track should have a reason to exist.]That said, I can't imagine any fan being disappointed by The Wow! Signal. It's got all the signature elements I personally love about this band: Matt Bellamy's passionate vocal style, the dramatic, ever-present tech and sci-fi vibes, Chris Wolstenholme's stellar bass work?especially on "Nightshift Superstar"?and plenty of wild electric guitar. Admittedly, my exposure to the band is still somewhat limited. I own Black Holes and Revelations and have done reaction videos to a number of their songs over the years, but I certainly wouldn't call myself an expert. I also love hearing the echoes of classical composers woven into Bellamy's songwriting.Muse has always excelled at creating a larger-than-life sound, and on this album that sense of scale is amplified by sweeping orchestral arrangements on several tracks?most dramatically on the opener, "The Dark Forest," which reminded me of epic film scores like Lawrence of Arabia and other grand cinematic works of that era.They're playing to their strengths as musicians and songwriters. Even a weaker track like "The Sickness in You and I" is partially redeemed by its strong chorus. On the other hand, there's a fair bit of progressive metal chugging that I'm sure fans of the genre will enjoy, but it strikes me as just a little out of place. It feels playful, almost as if the band is having fun with the style, but at times it comes across as something added to strengthen the track rather than something the song truly needed.The very pop-oriented track "Hush" (which, unsurprisingly, is not really my thing) features guest vocalist Ellie Goulding. It's a cool addition, and the song did grow on me somewhat, but I have to ask: is this really the direction Muse wants to pursue? I hope not.Lyrically, The Wow! Signal continues Muse's fascination with big ideas: technology, humanity's place in the universe, dystopian themes, and the tension between progress and consequence.I give the album 4 out of 5 dog bones. It's a pretty cool record, with enough diversity across the songs to eliver a satisfying platter of musical fun.
items._genre: progressive rock / alternative rock / cinematic rock / progressive metal
items._cn_summary: Muse的新作延续了乐队标志性的宏大叙事风格，弦乐编排与电吉他交织，营造出史诗般的电影感。Matt Bellamy的演唱充满戏剧张力，主题延续了对科技、人类命运与宇宙的探讨。专辑中部分曲目融入古典作曲家的影响，配合失重感的器乐编排，呈现出超越流行摇滚的剧场化气质。然而，评论者也指出部分曲目存在渐进金属段落略显生硬、流行化合作曲方向令人困惑等问题。整体而言，专辑在制作规模和氛围营造上表现出色，曲目多样性较高，但部分作品的编曲取舍仍有提升空间。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — One of the many modern Italian prog acts that has kept the classic 70s years alive by reviving itand making it relevant in the 21st century, the Cuneo based PANDORA emerged in 2005 as the fatherand son team of keyboardist Beppo Colombo and drummer / bassist / guitarist / flautist /keyboardist / vocalist Claudio Colombo who together set sail into the new frontiers of Italian progof the current millennium. Together with lead vocalist Corrado Grappeggia, this trio has embarked ona journey that has yielded four albums and crucial appraise. In addition to the core power trio, theband's debut release DRAMMA DI UN POETA UBRIACO (Drama Of A Drunken Poet) also featured guitaristChristian Dimasi who would soon depart after this album's release.A veritable rekindling of 70s spirit shines on this album that goes down memory lane with the RPIretro highway passing by classic greats such as PFM, Banco, Bigletto di Bronzo, Museo Rosenbach andothers but also finds new life with references to the melodic prog metal of bands like DreamTheater, neo-prog stalwarts IQ, Arena and Pendragon as well as the usual suspects of classicsymphonic prog, namely Yes and Genesis. Delivering an album of seven stealthy tracks culminatingwith the near 14-minute closing prog behemoth "Salto nel Bulo" that collectively slink past the 63-minute mark, DRAMMA DI UN POETA UBRIACO delivers everything a retro progger with a modern sheencould possibly hope for. It's as dramatic as the title suggests all the while tempering the classicmelodic sensibilities with a touch of contemporary contrast. The mix is intoxicating indeed.While the slow burn intro that features a collage of multilingual dialogue offers a rather clumsystart as the first impressions, the band quickly falls into place with the opening "Il GiudizioUniversale" quickly showcasing Claudio's percussive prowess in full form which perfectly augmentsthe classic RPI sounds to a much more magnanimous and technically infused level of competency.Likewise the strong songwriting advances new takes on classic melodic techniques that still soundexhilarating some half decade after the fact. Nice touches of heavy angular guitar riffing generatesan energetic drive that is unprecedented in the 70s even by the heavier bands such as Biglietto perl'Inferno however never reaching the true metal camp as a few acts such as early Procession or IlRevescio della Medaglia who dished out their Italian proto-metal. The beauty of this is that theintensity of the keys and subordinate instrumentation maintains a similar energetic ecstasy whichmakes this a compelling release on many levels..The album immediately picks up momentum and tracks like "March To Hell," "Cos� Come Sei" and themonstrosity "Pandora" take the band's technical wizardry and playing chops to the brink beforepulling back on the more contemplative palette cleanser "Breve Storia di San George" set to abreezier acoustic chill vibe however after an equally laid back intro, the crafty title track burstsback into the high energy stance that the band had maintained throughout the first half of the act.The album culminates with the epic sounding "Salto nel Bulo" which captures the band's most sweepingmovements from soft contemplative ballad-like motifs to the full heavy complex procedures thatelevates the band's technical abilities. Overall the album could've been edited down about 15minutes to be a cohesively satisfying journey where then meets now but as it is it's certainly aworthy modern day excursion into the world of 21st RPI that maintains good relations with theancestors.

items._cn_summary: Pandora是一支来自意大利库尼奥的现代前卫摇滚乐队，由键盘手Beppo Colombo与多乐器演奏家Claudio Colombo父子于2005年组建，首张专辑《Dramma di un Poeta Ubriaco》（醉酒诗人的戏剧）于2008年发行。乐评将其定位为意大利复古前卫摇滚（RPI）的复兴之作，音色与编排明显致敬PFM、Banco、Balletto di Bronzo、Museo Rosenbach等七十年代意大利经典乐队，同时融入Dream Theater式的旋律前卫金属元素以及IQ、Arena、Pendragon等新前卫乐队的风格。专辑共七首曲目，总时长超过六十三分钟，结尾是一首近十四分钟的长篇大作。键盘主导的织体配合Claudio的全方位打击乐与器乐演奏，构成技术性较强的复古取向作品，评论认为其成功之处在于将七十年代的经典旋律感与当代音色融合，形成兼具怀旧气质与现代张力的听觉体验，但对追求实验性、爵士即兴或电子声响探索的听众而言，该专辑仍属传统前卫摇滚范畴内的稳妥制作。

items.body: I've been writing for a while about the injection of ideas and sounds from shoegaze, indie, and alternative rock into post-rock and metal. I mean, the process has been going for decades now but it seems that another wave has hit us in the last two years or so. What I've yet to hear though is a doom band incorporating these same influences. On Cycles in the Infinite Dream, REZN appear to have done just that. While the bedrock of their sound is still there, namely thick guitar chords over dreamy atmosphere conjured forth by synths and evocative vocals, the flavor feels wholly different. The guitars are not as dominant and the structure of the tracks is less concerned with crushing as it is with unfurling. As a result, the atmospheric elements of REZN's sound take precedence and blend with ideas from the aforementioned genres.This is all great stuff by the way, if you were having doubts on where I stand. Cycles in the Infinite Dreams is the band's sixth release (depending on how you count) and comes on the heels of the excellent and successful Solace and Burden. While I adore those releases (and their earlier ones are also great), it's fantastic to hear something new from the band. "The Vessel" is probably my favorite track on the album. It showcases the new melodical layout of the album in a great way. It opens with a classic REZN riff, all doomy groove and presence. But along the halfway mark, we can find a chorus resplendent in a more somber guitar lead and adorned with a grungier, more melancholic main riff. Add in the vocals in a new, "thinner" mode (which is not a criticism, rather a description) and the picture coalesces into something new, more contemplative and open ended than the band's previous sound. This is capitulated upon a bit later with a passage I can compare to no one else but Karnivool.Like I mentioned above, the heaviness is still there for those of you who are worried. Check out "Cloudfall" for example and its extremely kick-ass main riff. The guitars and bass still know how to go when REZN want them to, delivering thick, redolent doom metal when the band want them too. In fact, I think Cycles in the Infinite Dream has some of the band's best riffs, perhaps due to the fact that they have more freedom, and obligation, to play around with how they are constructed. But on this track as well, the presence is not maintained throughout the track but rather used as just another element in the sound.The end result of all of this is an album that might disappoint any REZN conservatives out there (is that even a thing?) If you're looking for Burden 2.0, this is not that and I, for one, am very happy about that. I want REZN, who are one of my favorite doom metal bands in operation, to keep pushing their sound and see what else they have to say. On Cycles in the Infinite Dream, it seems as if they have plenty left in their vocabulary. The album shines with a fresh approach, one that is happy to jump into the current direction that many (if not all) bands in the space are taking. Cycles in the Infinite Dream by REZN
items._cn_summary: REZN的第六张专辑将doom metal的厚重riff与shoegaze、indie、另类摇滚的梦幻氛围相融合，吉他不再主导，氛围元素与合成器、人声取而代之，构成更内省开放的声音。结构从碾压式转向渐进展开，riff因新自由度而更佳，重量感仍存但仅作为音色之一。评论指出这是对前作风格的进化而非复制，对乐队保守派粉丝可能造成冲击，但整体展现出乐队仍有充足的表达空间。

items.body: Top PicksRezn – Cycles In The Infinite Dream (post-prog)If Cycles In The Infinite Dream had come out before we posted our Top 25 Albums of the Year So Far lists, it probably would have topped mine. This comes as a shock to me as much as it might to some of you. Previously, Rezn have professed a sludgier, doomier product. Here, though, they've taken a turn for more progressive pastures, resulting in a both a lighter and more engaging sound. Elder's Through Zero provides a popular point of comparison. However, there's also an almost uplifting, elated mournfulness to proceedings that reminds me of the first (superior) Pallbearer album, or even Pink Floyd, during its floatier sections—except they also throw a big, stonking Mastodon-style sludge-riff on the end of every other song as well. items.body:
DINTE’s 333 shell the soul-gripping, rootsy sway of a top Hortense Ellis cut, backed with Big Youth’s DJ version on the same rhythm.

Finally available at a nice price, compared with steep 2nd hand asks, the sweetly soul-piquing breeze of Hortense Ellis, and her harmonic backing, leavens the weight of Jimmy Radway’s mid ‘70s production on the outstanding A-side original, countered by the gruffness of Big Youth and the exaggerated bass bias of his ‘Tribulation’ version. Reliably flawless cuts, like everything on 333.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了牙买加歌手Hortense Ellis的一首根源雷鬼作品，以及DJ Big Youth在同一种伴奏节奏上演绎的版本。Ellis的演绎以甜美嗓音与和谐和声为特色，Jimmy Radway在七十年代中期的制作呈现出浓郁的根源雷鬼质感。Big Youth的版本则加入了他粗犷的演绎风格与低音的强调。333厂牌以合理价格再版发行，避开了二手市场的高价。这是一张品质可靠的雷鬼再版作品，主要面向该类型爱好者，与实验、前卫或电子等领域的探索关系不大。

items.body: This new EP paves the way for Antony's forthcoming full-length, Swanlights, taking its lead track from the album but supplying a further four non-LP recordings - one of which features none other than William Basinski.  'Thank You For Your Love' is a graceful, gospel-tinged ballad that swells up with horns and feverish expressions of gratitude as it wheels towards the chorus.  As it progresses, the song turns out to be one of Antony's most outwardly jubilant songs, making for a refreshingly unabashed upbeat entry into her catalogue.  Another new song, 'You Are The Treasure' takes on a beautiful minimalist piano part as once again Antony eloquently professes her affections for the addressee.  'My Lord My Love' might be a little more familiar, as it previously appeared as a bonus track on The Crying Light if you pre-ordered your copy from Secretly Canadian.  However, since Rough Trade released the album over here, this song's likely to be new to most of us Brits.  Next, Currituck Co. guitarist Kevin Barker plays on a cover of Bob Dylan's comparatively obscure 'Pressing On', a cut from his 1980 LP, Saved.  It's a beautiful arrangement that fleshes out Antony's wonderful vocal with the gentlest of picked guitar parts and the clockwork trundle of music box tones and what sounds like tuned percussion, or perhaps electric piano.  The EP closes with a second unusual cover: John Lennon's 'Imagine', featuring none other than Boomkat fave William Basinski.  Understandably, Antony leaves her piano in favour of a guitar accompanied rendition of the song, with Basinski supplying a strange, dissolved electronic backdrop that flickers and whirrs patiently in the background.
items._genre: art pop / chamber pop / gospel ballad / singer-songwriter
items._cn_summary: 这张EP是Antony and the Johnsons为新专辑《Swanlights》预热的过渡作品，收录一首专辑主打曲及四首非专辑曲目。主打歌是一首融合福音元素的优雅抒情曲，加入铜管编配，情绪高昂而外放。另一首新歌以极简钢琴为基底，展现细腻情感表达。EP还翻唱了Bob Dylan较为冷门的福音时期作品和John Lennon的《Imagine》，后者与实验电子音乐人William Basinski合作，以吉他伴奏搭配他提供的溶解式电子背景，呈现出梦幻而空灵的氛围。整体编曲精致，Antony的声线依然是核心，但音乐风格偏向室内流行与民谣抒情，与实验、前卫或电子领域距离较远，仅在Basinski的合作中触及一点实验边缘。

items.body:
Brixton beatmaker Omari Lyseight parades his mid-Atlantic bonafides on 'Digital', tapping MIKE, Earl Sweatshirt, Niontay and Lerado Khalil as well as locals like Jawnino and Jadasea.

One of the most impressive things about the Surf Gang stable is that it refuses to confine itself to New York City. evilgiane's collective is outward-looking in the best way, reaching across the country and across the pond to make connections between various local sounds that usually get left to chance. Lyseight's no stranger though; he's spent the last few years immersing himself in the US scene, producing for MIKE, Lucki, YL and others while keeping a foot firmly in South London. 'Digital' displays this constant motion, mixing up his production - that seems to have been inspired by everything from Bay Area bounce and vintage trap to grime and UK funky - and providing his collaborators with plenty to work with. 

MIKE, who we last heard from on the 'POMPEII // UTILITY' double album, sounds particularly comfortable slurring from the top of the dome over Lyseight's foggy synths on 'Like or Repost', and his sparring partner Earl Sweatshirt sinks his teeth into a rack of redlined 808 kicks and kinked flutes on 'Square'. 10k's Niontay's also more than comfortable following Winter's brilliant 'Soulja Hate Repellant' with the 8-bit banger 'Gotham City's Finest', maybe the mixtape's most replayable track. But Lyseight's closer collaborators put in the work, too: Jadasea cuts through distortion and interference on early highlight 'Detonate the Fuse' and Jawnino returns to Surf Gang with the anthemic 'drugsintheparty'.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Brixton制作人Omari Lyseight主导，汇集了MIKE、Earl Sweatshirt、Niontay等多位说唱艺人。制作上融合了湾区bounce、复古trap、grime和UK funky等多种风格元素，模糊的合成器音色与808鼓机形成层次感。Earl Sweatshirt在'Square'中展示了尖锐的说唱风格，Niontay的'Gotham City's Finest'则带有8-bit电子游戏音效的趣味。整体上，Lyseight展现了横跨大西洋的音乐视野，将英美两地的声音特质交织。然而，从实验音乐角度看，这张专辑仍属于当代说唱/嘻哈范畴内的风格探索，而非真正意义上的先锋实验。其制作精良且不乏创意，但对追求前卫即兴或抽象声响的听众来说，跨界深度尚有局限。

items.body:
Eglo co-founder & Rinse FM resident Alex Nut continues to come into his own as a producer with deep cuts of beatdown soul and broken beat sagely nodding in the direction of Dego, Waajeed, Theo Parrish.

Nut is feeling the funk three different ways on his 3rd solo EP issued in the past 12 months. His DJ-honed club instincts and feel for timeless soul feed forward into the lo-slung shimmy of ‘Bright’, glazing a Detroit-style house strut with harmonised and cut-up vocal motifs bathed in warmest keys, before lacing it with a skudgy acid line for later in the night on its ‘Re-FreQ’ mix. The heat keeps knees up, hips swivelling, on a classic Y2K West London broken beat flex mutual to his and Floating Points’ tastes, whereas ‘Duck Duck’ really dials it down to with a bed ways glyde in its velvet-clad bass and dreamily vapourised chords.

items._cn_summary: Alex Nut 是 Eglo 厂牌联合创始人和 Rinse FM 常驻 DJ，这张《The Heat EP》是他在十二个月内推出的第三张个人作品。整张EP围绕funk展开三条不同路径：开篇曲《Bright》以底特律风格house为骨架，叠加和声化的人声切片与温暖键盘，'Re-FreQ'混音版在此基础上注入酸性合成器线条以适配深夜舞池；第二首回归Y2K时期西伦敦broken beat律动，与Floating Points的美学取向形成呼应；终曲《Duck Duck》则收敛锋芒，以天鹅绒质感的贝斯线和雾化和弦营造出绵软氛围。整体制作体现了DJ视角的俱乐部直觉与永恒灵魂乐底蕴的结合，但本质上是根植于舞曲传统的常规作品，实验性有限。

items.body:
Complete audio recording of the ‘Turning’ concert, recorded live at The Barbican in London in November 2006.

The concert contains songs from the first three Antony And The Johnsons full length albums - ‘Antony And The Johnsons’, ‘I Am A Bird Now’ and ‘The Crying Light’ - as performed by an ensemble of musicians including Maxim Moston, Rob Moose, Julia Kent, Parker Kindred, Jeff Langston and Thomas Bartlett. Plus two rare Antony And The Johnsons studio recordings from that period.

items.body:
The most memorable moment of  Music, Fashion, Film  comes during its first track and lead single, "Rock Music." Musing that she thinks the dance floor is now dead,  Charli xcx  turned heads by ditching the party girl persona that had fuelled the culture upending  Brat . As an act of bear-baiting it worked, but in truth, the proclamation was to be taken no more seriously than James Murphy’s turn-of-the-century observation that the kids were selling their guitars to buy turntables, both absurd theses that ignore the immortality of these institutions. Determined to challenge the standards of legacy and fame, her eighth studio album and second of 2026 offers a set of buzzy guitar pop that retains her charm without leaning on euphoria as a crutch. 

The pace has changed, the personnel hasn't:  Music, Fashion, Film  was produced entirely by PC Music founder A.G. Cook and label regular Finn Keane, two longtime collaborators who are crucial within the Charli-Industrial Complex. The glimmering quality of their pop production is still present, like on the shining synth melodies of "Camera" or the deep warbling sub-bass on "Card Declined," but it's now locked behind a steady flow of Pixies-esque guitar crunch and drum machine automation.

The rough edges of the instrumentation feel authentic, perhaps even a little unvarnished. Cook and Keane's band  Thy Slaughter  has previously approached this style of rock music via electronic, but the atmosphere feels akin to the laid back ambience of French soft pop duo  Air , injected with alternative icon  Steve Albini 's sonic forthrightness.

Whether it's the little vocal chops on "Rock Music" or the watery delay that gives "Camera" its urgency, the production duo are able to find a lockstep synchronicity with Charli's droll existential musings about throwing it all away, the vanity of legacy and generally ruining everything about her life. Overall, there's a charm to Charli's songwriting, making it relatable to even the greatest cynics. 

"Wink Wink" brims with whimsical synth melodies and a catchy hook that starkly contrast the observational verses about aging out of the fast life ("I used to jump on trampolines with no underwear on / and now I basically just wear trousers"). Flexing similar muscle to  Brat  and  how i'm feeling now  staples like "Girl, so confusing" and "anthems," the experienced songwriter is able to wrest an uncharacteristically exciting pop tune from the depths of her anxieties and insecurities. 

In spite of a short runtime,  Music, Fashion, Film  leaves you craving more. Take "Yeah," a hilariously bare track even for the songwriter's standards. It's burdened by an aimlessness found in the first song a teenage garage pop punk band would write, thanks to its repetitive power chords and shallow lyric pool. For a popstar at her level, the urge to rip it up and start again is fresh, but not as fresh as it once was—you can only ride a self-destructive streak so far. 

By the time "Magic Metal Montana" rolls around, a clunky but sweet tribute to A.G. Cook, the diary-style lyricism wears thin. Though she's often been confrontational, her writing can feel particularly unfiltered on songs like "I'm Afraid," where she lays her emotions so bare that it can feel borderline juvenile, as anxieties and insecurities can often seem. "Sympathy Is A Knife" took a similar route to a better outcome. What these songs do achieve, however, is to humanise an artist whose persona became so supersized that it risked crushing the person under it. You come away with a sense that Charli needed to make this record for herself, as much as anyone else. 

Towards the end of  Music, Fashion, Film , cult favorite director David Cronenberg offers some words of advice: "As I was lying there on the sidewalk, I did not think about art, at all," the  Videodrome  director muses on "No One Lasts Forever." "It can turn out that, yes, some artists have created art that has really survived thousands of years…but experientially, they are dead." 

If this is Charli's way of shirking immortality and strategically wrapping her arms around  impermanence, then it worked. Little resembles a new pop classic, however. Will that be enough to satiate the new fans who, post- Brat , look to her as an oracle? Perhaps not. But it feels almost innovative for an artist at the peak of their success to ignore the rat race and create something unfamiliar. By presenting a more intimate set of material than the crossover hits that launched her to global It Girl in 2024, Charli appears to have faced down the deathly industry cogs that have chewed up and spit out so many before her.

Cook与长期合作者Finn Keane共同制作，试图从Charli xcx此前的电子舞曲路线转向吉他驱动的流行摇滚。制作上保留了合成器旋律与低频质感的闪光特质，但被Pixies式的吉他噪音与鼓机自动化节奏所包裹，呈现出Steve Albini式的直接感与法国Air乐队松弛氛围的结合。Charli的创作延续了她对名利虚妄与自我毁灭的戏谑观察，歌词在幽默与疲惫之间游走。然而评论指出，专辑虽然以吉他流行作为新鲜尝试，但部分曲目显得空洞且重复，缺乏足够的深度与原创性。整体定位是主流流行明星对摇滚类型的一次短期探索，在创新性与实验性方面并无突破。

items.body: Project Pitchfork, the Hamburg group that mixes dark wave, electro-industrial and EBM elements, released “Continuum Ride” on 23 July 2010 through Trisol. The album turns 16 this year. It followed “Dream, Tiresias!” (2009) and arrived a year ahead of “Quantum Mechanics” (2011), appearing on CD in a Digipak and as a limited two-CD-plus-DVD edition. Peter Spilles wrote, composed and produced “Continuum Ride” and handled lead vocals; Dirk Scheuber and Jürgen Jansen completed the band’s core line-up on the record, with Achim Färber and Carsten Klatte contributing additional live musicianship. Chris von Rautenkranz mastered the album at Soundgarden Tonstudio in Hamburg, monozelle.de created the artwork and Silent-View supplied the photography. The 12-track album runs “Way of the World,” “Stacked Visions,” “The Dividing Line,” “Endless Infinity,” “Dead Cities,” “Continuum,” “Beholder,” “Ghost of the Past,” “Supersonic Snakebite,” “Star Child,” “43rd Floor” and “Full Contact.” The band wrote “Continuum Ride” after their 2009 US tour; in an interview with Brutal Resonance, Peter Spilles connected the record’s harder, more destructive sound to the band’s impressions of Detroit’s derelict skyline during that trip. Trisol issued a video for the track “Beholder” to support the album, and reissued “Continuum Ride” as a limited two-LP-plus-two-CD set through Trisol in 2019. About Project Pitchfork Project Pitchfork started in Hamburg, Germany, where vocalist and composer Peter Spilles and keyboardist Dirk Scheuber began collaborating in 1989. The pair played their first concert in Hamburg in February 1990 and recorded the demo “K.N.K.A.” that same year. Their debut album “Dhyani” followed in May 1991, and 1992 brought both “Lam-‘Bras,” which introduced vocalist Patricia Nigiani, and “Entities.” In 1994 the band moved to Off Beat for “IO,” whose singles “Renascence” and “Carrion” brought them into the German charts. A year later they founded their own imprint Candyland Entertainment, issued “Alpha Omega” and supported Rammstein on selected tour dates. Jürgen Jansen joined as a permanent member for “¡Chakra:Red!” (1997), and the concept album “Eon:Eon” (1998) marked the band’s move to the EastWest major-label imprint. The 2000s added “Daimonion” (2001) and the “NUN” trilogy built around “Inferno” (2002), before the band returned to an independent footing with “Kaskade” (2005). By 2010 Project Pitchfork had moved to Trisol, releasing “Dream, Tiresias!” the year before “Continuum Ride.” “Quantum Mechanics” followed in 2011, then “Black” (2013), “Blood” (2014) and “Look Up, I’m Down There” (2016), the last marking the band’s 25th anniversary. The current line-up centres on Peter Spilles with Jürgen Jansen on keyboards and Achim Färber and Christian “Leo” Leonhardt on live drums; co-founder Dirk Scheuber left the group in 2021. “Continuum Ride” sits early in the band’s Trisol-era run, between the 2009 US tour that shaped its sound and the “Quantum Mechanics” album that followed it a year later.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章是关于德国汉堡乐队Project Pitchfork 2010年专辑《Continuum Ride》发行16周年的资讯性回顾，并非真正的乐评。文章罗列了专辑的制作人员、曲目列表、发行版本（Digipak、CD+DVD、黑胶再版），以及乐队的简要历史。文章提到专辑录制于2009年美国巡演之后，主创Peter Spilles将专辑更硬朗、更具破坏性的音色与巡演中底特律破败城市天际线的印象联系起来。Trisol厂牌为单曲《Beholder》发行了MV。整体内容属于纯新闻资料性质，缺乏对音乐本身的声音设计、编曲结构、艺术取向等层面的深度分析，信息量有限。

items.body: Project Pitchfork will celebrate 35 years as a band with the “35 Years in the Heart of Darkness” anniversary tour, 11 dates across Germany between October 16 and December 13, 2026. The November 14 concert at Kulttempel in Oberhausen has sold out, with a waiting list available for fans still hoping to attend; several other dates are also seeing strong demand. Fronted by Peter Spilles, the band will bring their catalogue back to stages across the country, joined throughout the run by fellow German darkwave act Oberer Totpunkt as support. The tour opens at Waschhaus in Potsdam and moves through Dresden, Erfurt, Chemnitz, Munich, Rostock, Langen, Oberhausen, Bielefeld and Hamburg before closing at MusikZentrum in Hanover on December 13. Tour dates for Project Pitchfork October 16 – Potsdam – Waschhaus October 17 – Dresden – Alter Schlachthof October 23 – Erfurt – Central Club October 24 – Chemnitz – Kulturbahnhof October 31 – Munich – Backstage Werk November 11 – Rostock – M.A.U. Club November 13 – Langen – Neue Stadthalle November 14 – Oberhausen – Kulttempel (Sold Out) November 15 – Bielefeld – LokWerk December 12 – Hamburg – Markthalle December 13 – Hanover – MusikZentrum About Project Pitchfork Project Pitchfork was formed in Hamburg, Germany, by Peter Spilles and Dirk Scheuber, who met in late 1988 and began working together as Project Pitchfork the following year. The duo picked the name at random from a dictionary. After Spilles had circulated a handful of self-distributed cassettes, the band played its first live show in Hamburg in February 1990 and released the demo “K.N.K.A.” that August. Their debut album, “Dhyani,” followed in May 1991, a release Side-Line covered again in 2026 when Trisol marked its 35th anniversary with a new black 2LP edition. The band’s second album, “Lam-‘Bras,” arrived in February 1992 and introduced Patricia Nigiani as a backing vocalist, followed six months later by third album “Entities” – reissued as a limited 2LP deluxe edition in an April 2026 Side-Line report. A switch to the Off Beat label produced 1994’s “Io,” which gave the band its first German chart entry and was followed by a lengthy tour. In 1995 Project Pitchfork founded their own label, Candyland Entertainment, releasing “Alpha Omega” the same year and later signing to major-label imprint EastWest for 1998’s “Eon:Eon,” whose singles brought the band television airplay and an Echo Award nomination for the video to “Steelrose.” Jürgen Jansen joined as a permanent member for 1997’s “¡Chakra:Red!” and remains in the band’s current lineup alongside Spilles. Project Pitchfork continued releasing albums through the 2000s and 2010s, including “Daimonion” (2001), “Kaskade” (2005), “Continuum Ride” (2010) and “Quantum Mechanics” (2011), the latter two also anniversary subjects of earlier Side-Line pieces. By 2011 the band had moved from Candyland to Trisol, the label under which they released “Black” (2013), “Blood” (2014) and “Look Up, I’m Down There” (2016) to mark their 25th anniversary. Co-founder Dirk Scheuber left the band in March 2021. Project Pitchfork’s most recent studio album, “Elysium,” released in 2024 as the closing chapter of a trilogy begun with “Akkretion” (2018), and the band toured Germany and the UK in support of it. The “35 Years in the Heart of Darkness” tour this autumn extends that momentum into a full anniversary run across Germany.

items._cn_summary: 这段乐评以高度文学化、几乎是私语式的日文书写呈现，作者用「自尊心破坏」「过呼吸」「物差し」「秤」等意象构筑出一种被量化、被消费、被废弃的心理压迫感，与专辑名「暴投/暴挙/暴徒」的暴力语义形成共振。文风偏向身体感知与精神状态的描写，几乎没有提供具体的音乐技法、编配结构或声音设计的分析。作为专辑评介，信息密度偏低，读者难以从中获取关于实际声响、器乐配置或制作逻辑的判断依据，但与暗潮、工业、实验类作品的氛围气质存在一定贴合。整体可视为情绪化、印象派的随笔式评论，适合作为氛围联想的补充阅读，而非系统性的乐评参考。

items.body: In August 1819, tens of thousands of working men and women gathered in St. Peter�s Field in Manchester to hear the politician Henry Hunt speak. They were difficult times, many still out of work after the Napoleonic wars, rising prices and low wages � and always those at the bottom of the heap suffering. Hunt was a famed orator, a man on the side of the people, able to stir and inspire with his voice. Although the gathering was peaceful, the size of the crowd terrified the magistrates, who panicked and imagined an uprising. They sent in half-trained dragoons and the cavalry, who rode down, slashed and killed without compunction or compassion. In the end, 18 died and up to 700 were wounded. It was a stain on the nation, an outrage; prompting Percy Shelley, one of the poetic giants of the age, to write The Masque of Anarchy , with its famous lines: �Rise like Lions after slumber / in unvanquishable number / She your chains to earth like dew / Which in sleep had fallen on you / Ye are many - they are few.� Peterloo, as people called it, remains one of the seminal events in English working-class history, one that Sean Cooney of the Young 'Uns has revisited for this album of original songs, which is lavishly presented in a book with contemporary letters, political cartoons and illustrations to create a multimedia event. It�s ambitious, no doubt about that, and he�s selected some great talent to help � guitarist Sam Carter, the almost ubiquitous fiddler/singer Eliza Carthy, Ben Nicholls supplying background and texture on various instruments, and the Lancashire industrial ballad singer Jennifer Reid, who doubles as narrator. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid For a small ensemble, they make a powerful noise. The songs capture the feel of the day; the anticipation and excitement at the summer gathering, the joy that turns to terror and flight as the troops charge, then the bitter, mournful aftermath, voiced some powerful melodies and very well-chosen images. As a writer, Cooney often focuses on the personal in the small tales of people like �Sam Bamford� and �Mary Fildes,� while the three short pieces that comprise �The Monkey Rides The Mare� capture the bluster and arrogance of the soldiers. Peter's Field by Sean Cooney, Eliza Carthy, Sam Carter, Jennifer Reid Cooney is a persuasive singer, and on this heartfelt project, he puts plenty of emotion into his voice. Having two other outstanding vocalists alongside him makes for a wonderful triple threat. In these days when governments across the world are cracking down on protest, this stands as a sobering and very timely reminder. It�s a history lesson, yes, but the detail of the history stays in the book, while the music creates a set of songs that will resonate and remain for a long time. Find the artist online. Further reading: The Young'uns - Tiny Notes (Review) Ben Nicholls - Duets

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑取材于1819年曼彻斯特彼得卢大屠杀，由Young 'Uns乐队的Sean Cooney创作，汇聚了小提琴手Eliza Carthy、吉他手Sam Carter等英国民谣圈艺人，以原创歌曲再现这一英国工人阶级历史上的重要事件。专辑以多媒体形式呈现，搭配同时代信件、政治漫画与插图，歌曲捕捉了集会当日的期待与恐惧，士兵的傲慢与事后的哀悼。Cooney的演唱富有情感，配合另外两位出色歌手形成三人声部力量。在全球各地政府打压抗议的当下，这张作品以音乐形式提供了沉重的历史提醒。整体属于英国传统民谣与历史叙事歌曲范畴，扎根于地方传统，与用户的实验、前卫、爵士、电子等口味存在明显距离。

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items._cn_summary: 这张现场专辑录制于1999年莱茵河畔的露天剧场，Dr. John以钢琴为核心，带领一支新奥尔良本土乐队呈现了一场融合节奏布鲁斯、 funk 与Mardi Gras狂欢传统的演出。曲目涵盖了新奥尔良经典与个人代表作，包括开场曲《Iko Iko》、融合巫毒意象的《I Walk on Guilded Splinters》以及Ear King的《Big Chief》。乐队编制简洁，以吉他、贝斯、鼓为核心支撑钢琴与人声，整体呈现传统根源音乐的现场活力。文中虽提到funknology与巫毒仪式感等元素，但音乐本体仍属传统新奥尔良风格范畴，与实验、前卫或电子方向关联较弱。演出现场的文化氛围与场地背景是文章的叙事重点，文字带有一定文化随笔色彩。

items.body: “Seu corpo que disfarça a tatuagem do desejo”: a body hiding the tattoo of desire. That is where “A Cor do que Eu Quero” opens, two people at close range, concealing things from each other anyway. Roberta Campos wrote it and sings it with Mari Froes, and it anchors Coisas de Viver a Dois, out 29 May 2026 on Sonora Digital: her album Coisas de Viver re-recorded as duets, one guest per song, with the band that toured it for a year. Campos comes from Caetanópolis, a small town in Minas Gerais, and has written for Brazilian radio and telenovelas for nearly two decades. Froes is younger, from Anápolis in Goiás; her version of “Vaitimbora” went round the world last year. They swap verses over Campos’s nylon-string guitar, Amanda Barbosa‘s drums kept low and close, Diogo Ville laying a wash of keys underneath, Jackson Lourenço and João Elbert filling in the edges on bass and electric guitar. When the chorus arrives they sing it together, close enough that the harmony feels like conversation. The song is about living with someone. Not the honeymoon part, the everyday part: desire, arguments, the way one sentence can change the mood of a whole house. Campos gets it into three words: “Palavras mudando tudo”, words changing everything. Listen to “A Cor do que Eu Quero” and stream Coisas de Viver a Dois HERE The post Daily Discovery: Roberta Campos x Mari Froes – A Cor do que Eu Quero appeared first on Rhythm Passport.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是巴西歌手Roberta Campos将个人专辑《Coisas de Viver》以二重唱形式重新录制而成的项目，每首歌邀请一位嘉宾合作。合作单曲《A Cor do que Eu Quero》由Mari Froes参与，以尼龙弦吉他为核心，键盘铺底，贝斯、电吉他和低调的鼓组构建轻伴奏。两位歌手交替演唱主歌，合唱部分在近距离的声线交融中产生对话感。歌词围绕两人共同生活的日常展开，聚焦欲望、争执与一句改变家中氛围的话语，以简短直白的葡语短句呈现情感转折。整体编曲克制内敛，呈现出巴西主流流行音乐温柔知性的气质，与实验、前卫、电子等方向相距较远。

items.body: Review by Nickmannion — In 1975 when cash is short but your burgeoning music passion is growing exponentially the then mail order record clubs "5 albums for �1" were one way to grow your collection. Yes this was one of my joining offers 5! And I still have the self same copy. I knew who Ginger Baker was, the Gurvitz brothers not so much, but backloading my knowledge, they came from Three Man Army (whose albums I now have) and this is BGA's debut album.I actually really rate this album and is the best of their three studio efforts although the retro released 'Live in Derby '75' is my favourite and well worth finding the cd.So, what we don't have is drum dominated Cream/Airforce-esque re-treads but a very much of its time 'serious' rock music. For those not there, there was no in between, it was either pop for the masses (mostly an utter utter waste of time) or 'progressive' (what today we would term as 'metal' back then was always considered progressive ie Sabbath and so forth). This album, maybe due to familiarity, conjures up 1975 from the first groove to the last fade which is just a bit marvellous. So we get, if not a mish mash, then different approaches to the then rock oeuvre, from the sophisticated blues of '4 Phil' (great guitarist Mr Gurvitz) to the extended 'rock opera' of 'Mad Jack' (not sure but there was a film called Death Race 2000 that came out about this time and the 'tale' of Mad Jack sums it up). Actually the other comparisons to this track are two SAHB songs..'The Tale of the Giant Stone Eater' and ' Hot City Symphony/Vambo'....and both bands were managed by Bill Fehilly so maybe there was some cross fertilisation with this template. Every days a school day huh? 'Memory Lane' gives Baker his spotlight...am no drummer but wow...'Help Me' the opener really rocks out but has the most proggy keys layers too. 'Love Is' does the one thing I can't abide...orchestration behind/as part of a rock/prog song...and the jagged Hendrix type blues rock of the riff does not need any enhancement ..ok?! 'Inside Of Me' is the track that grabs. A simple repeated guitar refrain over descending minor key backing is so so so 1975 and so so perfect. I Wanna Live Again is orchestrated newly divorced self pitying angst and the one that could be cut. 'Since Beginning' could turn up on a Gentle Giant album...yes really...minus any baroque GG leanings ...and is the most 'ambitious' track. I know we shouldn't be influenced by the time/place/memories this conjures up...I can even picture my favourite tea mug I used to hug and drink from when you sat and listened...and believe it or not young uns, did nothing else but listen ...to albums as we did way back when...and the inner double page 'poster' that used to be in Sounds magazine of Paul Kossoff that was above my stereo on the wall ...but am going to give this a 4 even if it is 3.6ish. Try the above mentioned live CD...they had a full time keyboard player and singer by then and I saw them on that tour...which is a better representation of the band.
items._genre: heavy prog / hard rock / blues rock
items._cn_summary: 这张1974年首张专辑展现了70年代英国重摇滚的典型面貌，由鼓手Ginger Baker与Gurvitz兄弟组成。乐评指出专辑并非鼓主导的Cream式翻版，而是严肃的摇滚音乐，融合了精致蓝调、带有歌剧叙事结构的摇滚曲目以及带有前卫合成器层次的硬摇滚段落。鼓手Baker在Memory Lane中获得展示空间，歌曲Help Me以progressive键盘层次开场，Inside Of Me以简约重复的吉他乐句配合下行小调构成最抓人的段落。评论将Mad Jack与同时期SAHB的作品进行比较，Since Beginning则具有Gentle Giant式的复杂结构。整体而言，专辑虽有管弦乐铺陈和部分前卫元素，但仍属于时代性主流摇滚范畴，在创新性和风格融合方面与实验音乐相距较远。

items.body:
Originally released in 1995, Rachel Goswell and Neil Halstead's Mojave 3 debut 'Ask Me Tomorrow' has finally been given the deluxe treatment - remastered by Abbey Road and back in print for the first time in years. 

It's hard to believe that 'Ask Me Tomorrow' appeared less than a year after 'Pygmalion'. Slowdive's last album flopped at the time, though - their fusion of waved electronica and shoegaze wouldn't really catch on until a few decades later, long after the band had splintered. And in their wake, Halstead and Goswell traded the sounds of deep space for something more earthy, drawing on their love of Bob Dylan and Townes Van Zandt to record a demo of country-tinged acoustic pop. The tape made its way to 4AD's Ivo Watts-Russell, and was quickly bumped up into a full album that's probably the band's most consistently enjoyable. 

Goswell and Halstead sound refreshingly comfortably making echoing, Lynchian alt-country - something that shouldn't be too surprising to anyone who obsessed over the windy, whimsical 'Pygmalion' fave 'Blue Eyed An' Clear'. And they're still trapped in the shadow of shoegaze past on their debut, obscuring their vocals with reverb and slowing their songs down to a sensual crawl. Opener 'Love Songs on the Radio' lies between Slowdive and Mazzy Star and Goswell has rarely sounded better, while Halstead sounds almost like Nick Drake on the charming 'You're Beautiful'. The best is saved for last: 'Mercy', the album's dark, melancholy finale that sounds as if it's waving goodbye to an era that's already disappeared.
items._cn_summary: Mojave 3 1995年首张专辑由Abbey Road重新母带处理后再度发行。乐队由Slowdive解散后的核心成员Neil Halstead与Rachel Goswell组建，从前作飘渺的太空电子shoegaze转向根植于Bob Dylan与Townes Van Zandt影响的乡村色调原声流行。整张专辑笼罩在混响营造的迷雾中，延续了shoegaze余韵，节奏放缓至近乎感官爬行。Goswell在开场曲中展现出Slowdive至Mazzy Star之间的细腻唱腔，Halstead的嗓音则带有Nick Drake式的忧郁气质。终曲Mercy以深沉忧郁收束，仿佛在为一个已然消逝的时代告别。

items.body:
Ambitious but still as dreamy as their earliest gear, Mojave 3's third album snapshots a band in transition.

Nowhere near as glossy as its successors 'Spoon and Rafter' and 'Puzzles Like You', 2000's 'Excuses for Travellers' finalises Neil Halstead and Rachel Goswell's flirtations with country and folk by reining in their ambitions, aiming for reliability rather than experimentation. Sadly, Goswell doesn't get much chance to shine, but when she does appear on 'Bringin' Me Home'  it's a good reminder of how effective her voice is in almost any context. Backed by some synth from none other than Mark Van Hoen, she provides a much-needed palette cleanser and high point that sadly wasn't expanded on.

items.body:
Mojave 3's final album, released in 2006, 'Puzzles Like You' is a slick, sunny break from their reverberating early albums.

Undoubtedly the most controversial album in Rachel Goswell and Neil Halstead's Mojave 3 catalog, 'Puzzles Like You' didn't feel exactly like the end of an era when it appeared, but the start of a new one. By this time in the band's evolution, the traces of Slowdive had completely disappeared - which made it all the more surprising when the band re-formed in 2014, effectively ending Mojave 3 for good.

Going back now though, knowing how everything worked out, it's interesting to hear how Goswell and Halstead were motivated to keep up with a shifting industry, reacting to indie's forward motion by kissing goodbye to shoegaze mere moments before they'd become flavor of the month again.
items._cn_summary: 这是Mojave 3乐队2006年发行的最后一张专辑，是对其早期回响式作品的明显转向。乐队彻底脱离了Slowdive时期标志性的自赏派吉他音墙，转向明亮流畅的流行化编曲，呈现出阳光感更强的清爽质感。主创Rachel Goswell与Neil Halstea在此时试图回应独立音乐场景的演变方向，主动告别自赏派标签，尽管这一风格后来又重新流行。文章指出此作在当时并未被视为终章，反而预示着新阶段的开始，但乐队2014年重组后Mojave 3实际上已不复存在。整张专辑的创作动机更偏向对行业趋势的适应，而非声音实验的内在驱动。

items.body:
Green Gartside and co’s addictively sugary turning point album crops up for a masterclass in blue-eyed soul styles.

Upon its release in 1985, ‘Cupid & Psyche 85’ marked a radical leap for the once squat dwelling communists from new wave dreamers to chart-worthy pop pucker. Prior to this record they had markedly political and philosophical leanings set to a mix of almost folksy whims, disco and reggae lite, as found on a handful of Rough Trade releases, but with ‘Cupid & Psyche 85’ they mounted a sly assault on the charts, drawing on Green Gartside’s love of Aretha Franklin’s aching soul for a far more polished sound that would parallel the likes of Prefab Sprout’s entry to the US billboard charts.

In many ways its not hard to draw lines between Gartside and the Sprout’s Paddy McAloon; both are reclusive genius types who saw the other side of the pop machine and disliked it, and both made some of the ‘80s greatest power moves, as Scritti Politti did with the likes of ‘Absolute,’ which now uncannily reminds us of trotting around Co-Op during early lockdown (it was on their in-store radio A-list), and the natty funk of ‘Wood Beez,’ their seminal prayer for Aretha Franklin, which is coincidentally co-produced by Arif Mardin.
items._genre: blue-eyed soul / synth-pop / new wave pop
items._cn_summary: Scritti Politti在1985年发行的这张专辑标志着重大的风格转型，从早期Rough Trade厂牌时期带有政治哲学色彩、融合民谣、迪斯科与雷鬼元素的创作，转向更精致的流行灵魂乐。制作上明显受Aretha Franklin影响，单曲如《Absolute》和《Wood Beez》展现了流畅的放克节奏与细腻的编曲，后者更由传奇制作人Arif Mardin联合制作。整张专辑体现了对排行榜的策略性进军，Green Gartside与Paddy McAloon一样，以内敛的创作姿态在八十年代主流乐坛留下了独特的作品。然而，就音乐本质而言，这是一张高度精致的主流流行灵魂乐唱片，制作取向明确指向商业成功，与实验、前卫、暗潮或电子等非常规音乐路线相距甚远。

items.body: Review by Matti — (Revisiting my Colossus reviews from 2013, pt. 4)At the time of receiving this CD I simultaneously got one that introduced me to the New York based prog band IZZ, a member of which John Galgano has always been. What surprises me now, 13 years later, is that this has remained his sole solo album, and without a single review! In my brief original review I even speculated if this young-looking guy could become one of the most promising solo artists in the American prog scene. Well, that didn't happen. John Galgano's main instrument in the multi-vocal group IZZ is the bass. Here he plays also guitars and some keyboards. Two of the shorter songs he co-wrote with his wife and IZZ colleague Laura Meade whose vocals are heard on most tracks. This feature increases the obvious similarities to IZZ. There are however less keyboards, and perhaps several pieces have a more intimate atmosphere and less of the rollercoaster prog eclectism. Overall it's easy to hear this is American prog, with kindred spirit to the likes of Spock's Beard and Glass Hammer. Lots of vocal harmonies and a sharp production. The album deals with the tough question of being human in modern times. The brief, small-scale opener has only John's vocals and acoustic guitar. The five norm-length songs operate between pop accessibility and a little prog complexity in rhythmic structures and sonic colours. The heavily repetitive chorus on 'Bigger on the Inside' is less elegant than the rest of the song. 'Lucky for Me' is entirely sung by Laura, nice. 'This Is How It Happens' is an emotional highlight in its somber intimacy. I don't like the alienating way how Laura's vocals are treated on 'The Only Thing' but there are interesting details in the arrangement, as well as on the more energetic 'Look Around'.'1000' is a 19-minute, multi-part epic with a higher degree of eclectic variety and dynamics. While Galgano respects the 70's rooted symphonic prog tradition, his music always sounds contemporary 21st century prog rock. The guitar sound on some movements owes especially to Steve Howe. Again the vocals are treated here and there. The album's official outro is a Pt. 2 of the title track, but after that comes a hidden track, a beautiful but disappointingly short a cappella piece revisiting the song 'This Is How It Happens'. This is a fine album which definitely should have gained more attention. Four stars, although I wish there were more notable instrumentally oriented sections throughout the album, not only in the epic.
items._genre: crossover prog / symphonic prog / american prog
items._cn_summary: John Galgano的首张也是唯一一张个人专辑，由IZZ贝斯手独立完成，除贝斯外还演奏吉他和部分键盘。大部分曲目由他与妻子Laura Meade共同创作，Laura在多数曲目中担任主音。专辑主题围绕现代生活中的人性困境展开，作品介于流行可听性与节奏结构上的轻度前卫复杂性之间。开场曲简短克制，仅用人声与原声吉他；五首中等长度歌曲在流行与前卫间游走，合唱部分的人声和声层次丰富，制作锐利。19分钟的多乐章长篇作品是专辑重心，展现出更高的折衷主义多样性与动态变化，吉他音色向Steve Howe致敬。整体仍属七十年代根源的交响前卫传统范畴，但呈现的是二十一世纪当代声响。部分歌曲的人声处理方式略显疏离，但编曲细节仍有可观之处。

items.body: Review by Matti — (Revisiting my Colossus reviews from 2013, pt. 3)The organ loaded proto proggers The Gods were Ken Hensley's group before Uriah Heep. Due to the quickly changing line-up The Gods also makes references to King Crimson (Greg Lake) and Jethro Tull (John Glascock plays the bass on this album), and even to the Rolling Stones. I bet quite a many second-hand vinyl store customer has at first, for a second, wondered if "Genesis" contains early stuff of Peter Gabriel, Tony Banks and co. The listening experience is pretty ambivalent nevertheless.Energetic early heavy rock with plenty of vocal harmonies, all right! But before long all that, spiced up by psychedelic inter-speeches, is bursting out from the other ear. Hensley's, or the whole quartet's, skills at songwriting frankly weren't very mature yet. Esoteric's 2-CD reissue contains both stereo and mono version of the album plus four rather weak single tracks.
items._cn_summary: 这张1968年的唱片由The Gods乐队录制，被归类为前卫摇滚的早期雏形。乐队成员后来分别加入了Uriah Heep、King Crimson和Jethro Tull等知名乐队。专辑以风琴为驱动，融合了早期重金属摇滚的能量感与人声和声，并穿插迷幻风格的段落。乐评指出，作曲技巧在彼时尚未成熟，音乐品质呈现两极化：一方面充满活力和感染力，另一方面整体深度有限。Esoteric厂牌的双CD再版收录了立体声与单声道版本以及四首品质平平的单曲。作为Proto-Prog的代表作品，它更多具有历史文献价值，在创新性和艺术深度方面并未达到成熟前卫摇滚的水准。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items.body: Review by Nickmannion — In one of those 'coincidences' that life throws up, I went to the same school as Norm Barratt but was 9 or 10 years younger (and am not sure about Gravy Train forming in Manchester as he lived nearer Liverpool but I digress...) and in the summer term of '74 school, who had quite a big hall and stage at one end, gave out free tickets for 'a concert' where a group including an ex pupil (yup..) were going to film themselves playing to us the audience, for promo purposes and now , I also assume, for this album in particular*. Long story short, the electrics couldn't cope with the back line/PA/lights and film gear and they blew. The band ended up miming to probably this album and the whole thing fell a bit flat. I can't even get to say I saw them 'live' although at the time I had no idea who they were and if it wasn't Sabbath or Purple I can't say I would have been impressed either...well, you know, we have all been 14/15...Yes I now know full well who they are/were and am reviewing this album first (I have them all) due to the above. I have got a cd copy as my vinyl was a bit battered and never found one priced 'at my worth' to upgrade, hence the cd replaced it. It does have 'bonus tracks' which I will dismiss here as utterly dire, from when NB went all Xian 'rock' and never get played.OK the album itself. Hmmmm. My least favourite of theirs and in summary a cross between BJH and Fruupp fronted by Demis Roussos...unfortunately in his Euro pop cross over period and not his time in Aphrodites Child...and BJH and Fruupp not on a good day either. I may be misremembering but I think the film above was for the American market as the flyers/tickets stated and maybe this is why this album is less than inspiring and what you might called 'watered down'. The title track is the best example and has a fair few prog influences that are sort of skirted with (other than the two I have mentioned)...maybe Greenslade and Supertramp being others... but it doesn't get out of 1st gear and the vocals (see comparison above) are over wrought and could have been fronting a non British '74 Eurovision entry. And comparing it to their wilder Tull twisted heavy blues drenched first effort say, it just leaves me non plussed. It certainly 'ain't heavy' and maybe an already out of their time band having one last throw of the dice at 'success' hence the compromises. Sorry Norm but even though we share an alma mater, I can't rate this album too high and it has not aged well. Yes I would probably go 2.75 but it isn't 'good' so I cannot give it a 3. * I have scoured the net and found no footage anywhere so it probably got binned or, with the electrics issue, they may not have got anything on celluloid either...but it did happen!

items.body: Beethoven completed his Piano Sonata No. 14 in 1801 and published it the following year, one of a pair issued under the heading quasi una fantasia, meaning in the manner of a fantasy. He dedicated it to a young pupil, the Countess Giulietta Guicciardi. The famous “Moonlight” name was not the composer’s own. It came from a later writer, the poet Ludwig Rellstab, whose image of moonlight on a still lake gave the piece its lasting nickname. The name stuck so firmly that the sonata is now among the most played of all piano works, known less for the storm of its finale than for the stillness of its opening. The sonata breaks with convention by placing its weight at the end rather than the start. It opens not with a bright sonata-allegro but with a slow, veiled Adagio, its steady triplets and muted sonority holding to a single subdued mood. A short, graceful Allegretto follows, a brief lightening between the darkness on either side. Then comes the Presto agitato, a stormy finale in full sonata form that carries the real drama of the piece and makes the greatest demands on the player. Beethoven asked that the whole first movement be played with the sustaining pedal held down, so the harmonies blur into a soft, resonant halo that pianists still balance in different ways. Some lean into Romantic atmosphere and rubato, others into classical clarity of line, and a few turn to the lighter fortepiano of Beethoven’s own day. That is where these recordings part company. Here are The Classic Review editorial team’s recommendations for the best recordings of Beethoven’s Piano Sonata No. 14 (“Moonlight”). Murray Perahia Perahia’s is among the most carefully considered accounts on the list, prepared from his own close study of the score. He opens the first movement softly and without hurry, holding a steady pulse that neither drags nor presses, and he runs the three movements together as a single arc. The gentle Allegretto arrives like light breaking after the shadowed opening. His finale is fluent and cleanly fingered, though it stays a shade more contained than the stormiest versions here. This is a refined, unforced Moonlight for listeners who prize clarity over drama. Read the full review of this album here Perahia Amazon Presto Apple Emil Gilels Gilels brings a serene composure to the Moonlight that sets it slightly apart from the more volatile readings here. His first movement is quiet and beautifully weighted, the triplets kept level and the tone never pressed, so the music settles into something close to a slow hymn. He carries that same control into the finale, shaping its agitation with a firm hand rather than letting it run wild. Few pianists match the evenness of his touch or the depth of his sound. Gilels Amazon Presto Apple Arthur Rubinstein Rubinstein came to this sonata late and recorded it in his mid-seventies, and the playing has the ease of a man with nothing left to prove. He keeps the opening plain, with only the slightest give in the pulse, so the line stays grave rather than sentimental. He gives unusual care to the little middle movement, which many pianists treat as a throwaway between the outer two. The finale is steady and clear without being driven hard. This is the Moonlight of a grand lyric style, warmer and less austere than Brendel. Rubinstein Amazon Presto Apple András Schiff Recorded live, Schiff’s account puts the score itself first. His first movement flows more freely than most, taken at a gentle two beats to the bar so it moves forward. He follows Beethoven’s own veiling of the sound closely, blending the harmonies under a sustained pedal. When the finale arrives he meets its drama head on, and the concert setting lends the outburst an extra charge. It thinks harder about the letter of the score than almost any reading here, yet still remains highly controversial. Schiff Amazon Presto Apple Maria João Pires This is the first of Pires’s two recordings of the sonata, and the more direct of the pair. Where her later remake grew slower and more inward, here she is quicker and plainer-spoken, letting the first movement move without lingering over its atmosphere. The reading has a clean, unfussy line and a bright clarity well suited to the music’s fantasy marking. Her finale is fleet and lightly sprung rather than heavy. It offers a fresher, more classical view than the weightier readings around it, and it wears that directness well. Pires Amazon Presto Apple Paul Lewis Lewis takes a cool, refined view, smoothing away the roughness that some pianists press into the music. His tone is beautifully graded and his fingerwork suave, and he shapes the sonata more through color and texture than through changes of speed. The playing is at its most personal in the little Allegretto, which he draws out with slight lingerings and soft swells of dynamic. Few here are as polished or as finely finished. Lewis Amazon Presto Apple Ronald Brautigam Brautigam plays a fortepiano of Beethoven’s own day, and it changes the whole character of the piece. The lighter action and bell-like upper register clear away the thick Romantic haze, so the first movement sounds spare and eerie rather than merely dreamy. Freed of that weight, his tempos are brisk and his manner refreshingly free of sentiment. The real payoff is the finale, which fairly crackles, every note of the fast figuration clear and biting in a way a modern grand can blur. For anyone curious how this music sounded on the pianos of Beethoven’s time, it is the essential choice. Brautigam Amazon Presto Apple Alfred Brendel Brendel recorded the Moonlight three times, and this is the second, from the 1970s. It is a reserved, patient reading, closer in spirit to the classical poise than to overt Romantic feeling. Everything is weighed and clearly voiced, the structure always audible beneath the surface. Set beside the warmer readings here it can seem sober, and it gives up its rewards slowly. This is a thinking musician’s Moonlight, one of the most searching first movements on the list. Brendel Amazon Presto Apple Maurizio Pollini Pollini approaches the Moonlight with an analyst’s clarity, every strand of the texture cleanly separated. He uses notably little pedal in the first movement, so the harmonies never cloud over, yet the line stays relaxed and singing rather than cold. It is in the finale that his command really tells. The rushing arpeggios come through with a hard, glinting brightness, each one struck distinct, over a left hand that holds the music to an unusually firm tread. Warmth and mystery are not really his aim here. For control and transparency, though, few on the list rival him. Pollini Amazon Presto Apple Stephen Kovacevich Kovacevich draws the sharpest contrast here between the sonata’s two extremes. His first movement is among the most tender on record, the murmuring triplets kept soft and even, its small climaxes swelling and receding without ever breaking the calm. Then he throws himself into the finale, one of the most violent ever set down. The racing arpeggios stay crisp and distinct, and the great hammered chords hit hard without turning to mere noise. Nothing spills into chaos, though. It is a thrilling, tightly held reading. Kovacevich Amazon Presto Apple Bonus Choice: Benno Moiseiwitsch Moiseiwitsch belonged to the grand Romantic school of pianism, and this 1941 recording sounds like it. He plays with a freedom that few would risk today, bending the pulse and voicing the melody with a singer’s instinct. The famous opening is unhurried and finely colored, its rubato applied with a light hand rather than pulled about. The sound is plainly of its era, but the poetry comes through undimmed. It stands here as a reminder of an older, more personal way of playing Beethoven that the later readings, for all their polish, do not attempt. items.body:
KATSEYE have returned with a fierce new single. The global girl group unveiled 'Animal', a flirtatious pop anthem that explores the contrast between the polished personas people present to the world and the uninhibited versions of themselves behind closed doors.

Co-written by Ed Sheeran and produced by Omer Fedi and Blake Slatkin, the track pairs magnetic pop production with playful lyricism, transforming themes of secrecy, attraction, and impulse into an empowering statement. 'Animal' serves as the latest preview of WILD, the group's third EP, which is set for release on 14 August via HYBE x Geffen Records.

The accompanying music video leans into the song's duality, unfolding across observation rooms, mirrored realities, and shifting identities. Directed by Cody Critcheloe — who also helmed the group's 'Gnarly' and 'Touch' visuals — the cinematic clip features dynamic choreography, surreal imagery, and a cameo from Academy Award-nominated actress Demi Moore.

'Animal' follows KATSEYE's first single of the WILD era, 'PINKY UP', which the group debuted live during their Coachella performance. Fans can also look forward to KATSEYE: WILD HEARTS, a limited theatrical release beginning 12 August, ahead of the group's sold-out KATSEYE: THE WILDWORLD arena tour, which kicks off on 1 September.

items.body:
JENNIE is ushering in a softer side of her artistry with the release of her new single, 'Less than a Lover', out now via ODDATELIER/Columbia Records.

Serving as an ode to summer, the alternative-pop track captures the lingering emotions of a relationship that exists somewhere between friendship and romance. Written by JENNIE herself, 'Less than a Lover' pairs lo-fi guitar textures and vintage electric keyboards with intimate vocals as she reflects on the excitement and uncertainty of an undefined connection.

The accompanying music video, based on a story by JENNIE, follows the BLACKPINK star as she steps into another version of herself while filming a short movie with friends. As the fictional romance unfolds on set, the lines between performance and reality begin to blur, reshaping the dynamic between the characters.

The singer first previewed 'Less than a Lover' during her headline performance at Governors Ball in June, before bringing the track to festival audiences at Mad Cool, Open'er and Roskilde. Next, she is set to headline Lollapalooza Chicago before making her debut at Summer Sonic in Japan.

As one of pop's defining global stars, JENNIE continues to expand her artistic range through music, performance and creative storytelling. With 'Less than a Lover', she leans into a more understated sonic palette while exploring the complexities of connections that don't fit neatly into labels.
